# Feature Catalog: Gap — Memory & Knowledge System

> **Series**: 1800
> **EPICs**: EPIC-1800 (Memory System), EPIC-1810 (Memory Storage & Retrieval), EPIC-1820 (Knowledge Integration)
> **Gap Source**: diegosouza-omniroute (memory extraction, injection, retrieval, summarization, store with vector search)
> **Total Features**: 30

## Gap Analysis Summary

Our catalog has no features related to a persistent memory system. The diegosouza reference implements a full memory system with:
- **Memory extraction** — automatically extract notable facts, preferences, and context from conversations
- **Memory injection** — inject relevant memories into new conversations as context
- **Memory retrieval** — vector-similarity-based memory search
- **Memory summarization** — summarize and deduplicate memories over time
- **Memory store** — persistent storage with vector search capability

This is a significant gap for any system aspiring to support agentic workflows where context persists across sessions.

## Classification Guide

- **EXTENDED**: Core memory system — valuable for agentic use cases but not required for basic gateway
- **ECOSYSTEM**: Advanced memory features (auto-summarization, knowledge graphs)

---

## Features

### Memory System Core (1800-1809)

| # | Name | Description | Classification | Priority | Proposed EPIC |
|---|------|-------------|---------------|----------|---------------|
| 1800 | Memory Domain Model | Define `Memory` entity: ID, subject (user/session), key, content, embedding vector, source (conversation ID), tags, relevance score, created, updated, expires | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-1800 (new) |
| 1801 | Memory Repository | Implement `MemoryRepository` — Create, GetByID, Search (vector similarity), List by subject, Update, Delete with PostgreSQL + pgvector extension | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-1800 |
| 1802 | Memory Extraction | Implement memory extraction: analyze conversation turns, identify notable facts/preferences/instructions, create memory entries automatically | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-1800 |

# Feature Catalog: Gap — Webhooks & Events

> **Series**: 1900
> **EPICs**: EPIC-1900 (Webhook Dispatcher), EPIC-1910 (Event Subscriptions), EPIC-1920 (External Notifications)
> **Gap Source**: diegosouza-omniroute (HMAC-signed webhook delivery, 7 event types, exponential backoff)
> **Total Features**: 25

## Gap Analysis Summary

Our catalog has an event bus skeleton (1B4-1B5), outbox pattern (1B0-1B3), SSE admin events (1100-1109), and budget alert webhook (81D at P2). However, we lack:

- **External webhook dispatcher** — delivering events to external HTTP endpoints
- **Webhook HMAC signing** — cryptographic verification of webhook authenticity
- **Webhook retry management** — exponential backoff, dead letter queue
- **Webhook subscription management** — per-subscriber event type filtering, URL configuration
- **Webhook delivery tracking** — delivery status, retry history, failure alerts

The diegosouza reference has a full webhook system with 7 event types, HMAC-signed delivery, and exponential backoff retry.

## Classification Guide

- **CORE**: Webhook dispatcher with HMAC signing — needed for external integration
- **EXTENDED**: Advanced delivery management, dead letter queue, subscription filtering
- **ECOSYSTEM**: Webhook marketplace, third-party integrations

---

## Features

| # | Name | Description | Classification | Priority | Proposed EPIC |
|---|------|-------------|---------------|----------|---------------|

# Feature Catalog: Gap — Provider Ecosystem

> **Series**: 2000
> **EPICs**: EPIC-2000 (Tier-1 Provider Adapters), EPIC-2010 (Tier-2 Provider Adapters), EPIC-2020 (Self-Hosted/Local Providers), EPIC-2030 (Embedding & Specialty Providers)
> **Gap Source**: diegosouza-omniroute (160+ providers; we only plan OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, OpenRouter, Generic)
> **Total Features**: 40

## Gap Analysis Summary

Our catalog defines 6 provider adapters: OpenAI (710-719), Anthropic (720-729), OpenRouter (730-734), Generic OpenAI-Compatible (736-738), Google Gemini (740-745), and Groq (746-749). The diegosouza reference supports 160+ providers.

We do NOT need to build 160+ adapters. Most providers speak OpenAI-compatible API and can use our Generic adapter (736). However, several **tier-1 and tier-2 providers** have unique APIs, authentication patterns, or important market share that warrant dedicated adapters or at least documented configuration for the Generic adapter.

### Prioritization Criteria
1. **Market share and usage** — providers developers actually use
2. **API uniqueness** — providers with non-OpenAI-compatible APIs
3. **Strategic importance** — local/self-hosted, enterprise cloud, specialty

## Classification Guide

- **CORE**: Tier-1 providers with unique APIs (Mistral, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, DeepSeek) — needed for enterprise adoption
- **EXTENDED**: Tier-2 providers, self-hosted (Ollama, vLLM), embedding-only providers
- **ECOSYSTEM**: Long-tail providers that work via Generic adapter

---

## Features

### Tier-1 Provider Adapters (2000-2009)

|---|------|-------------|---------------|----------|---------------|

# Feature Catalog: Gap — Advanced Caching

> **Series**: 2100
> **EPICs**: EPIC-2100 (Signature & Prompt Cache), EPIC-2110 (Request Deduplication & Idempotency), EPIC-2120 (Reasoning Cache)
> **Gap Source**: diegosouza-omniroute (signature cache, prompt cache, reasoning cache, request dedup, idempotency layer)
> **Total Features**: 25

## Gap Analysis Summary

Our catalog has a semantic cache system (870-879) covering exact-match caching,  cache key generation, TTL strategies, and embedding-based similarity cache. We also have workload fingerprinting (617), classification caching (618), and request deduplication (784 at P2). However, we lack:

- **Signature cache** — content-aware request dedup beyond simple hash matching
- **Prompt cache** — deduplicate identical system prompts across requests (50 entries, 2MB, 5min TTL)
- **Reasoning cache** — cache and re-inject reasoning/thinking content across turns
- **Full idempotency layer** — `X-Request-Id` / `Idempotency-Key` based dedup with storage
- **Request coalescing** — coalesce concurrent identical requests into single upstream call

These are orthogonal to our existing semantic cache and represent important optimization layers.

## Classification Guide

- **CORE**: Idempotency layer, request dedup/coalescing — essential for production reliability
- **EXTENDED**: Prompt cache, signature cache, reasoning cache — optimization features

---

## Features

### Signature & Prompt Cache (2100-2109)

| # | Name | Description | Classification | Priority | Proposed EPIC |
|---|------|-------------|---------------|----------|---------------|
| 2100 | Signature Cache | Implement content-signature cache: generate signature from normalized request content (model + messages + params), deduplicate identical requests within configurable window | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-2100 (new) |
| 2101 | Signature Generation | Generate request signatures: normalize request (sort params, trim whitespace, canonicalize messages), hash with BLAKE3; signature used for dedup and cache lookup | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-2100 |
| 2102 | Prompt Cache | Implement prompt cache: cache system prompts by content hash; when same system prompt appears in multiple requests, reuse cached token count and preprocessing | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-2100 |
| 2103 | Prompt Cache Limits | Enforce prompt cache limits: max entries (default 50), max total size (default 2MB), TTL (default 5min); LRU eviction | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-2100 |
| 2104 | Prompt Cache Key | Generate prompt cache key: hash of system prompt content + model; different models may tokenize differently | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-2100 |
| 2105 | Provider Prompt Caching | Forward provider-side prompt caching hints: OpenAI `cached_prompt_tokens`, Anthropic `cache_creation_input_tokens`; track cache savings | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2100 |
| 2106 | Cache-Aware Cost Calculation | Adjust cost calculation for cache hits: provider-cached prompts cost less (Anthropic: 10% of normal), track savings separately | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2100 |
| 2107 | Cache Layer Hierarchy | Implement cache layer hierarchy: L1 local in-memory (sub-ms) → L2 Redis (1-5ms) → L3 cache miss (upstream); configurable per cache type | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2100 |
| 2108 | Cache Warming | Support cache warming: precompute cache entries for known-frequent requests (scheduled or trigger-based) | ECOSYSTEM | P3 | EPIC-2100 |
| 2109 | Signature Cache Tests | Test suite for signature and prompt caching: key generation, hit/miss, eviction, TTL, cost savings tracking | EXTENDED | P2 | EPIC-2100 |

### Request Deduplication & Idempotency (2110-2119)

| # | Name | Description | Classification | Priority | Proposed EPIC |
|---|------|-------------|---------------|----------|---------------|

# Feature Catalog: Gap — A2A Agent Protocol

> **Series**: 2200
> **EPICs**: EPIC-2200 (A2A Protocol Core), EPIC-2210 (Agent Cards & Skills), EPIC-2220 (A2A Task Management)
> **Gap Source**: diegosouza-omniroute (A2A protocol, JSON-RPC 2.0, task manager, agent card, skills), cybernetics-core (agent profiles registry, skills registry)
> **Total Features**: 30

## Gap Analysis Summary

Our catalog defines A2A-related domain types (`ExposureKindA2ASurface` at 135, P2) and A2A surface exposure config (343, P2) but lacks the actual A2A protocol implementation. The diegosouza reference has a working A2A implementation with JSON-RPC 2.0, task management, and agent cards. The cybernetics-core reference adds agent profiles with ratings, reviews, cloning, and favorites, plus a skills registry with discovery marketplace.

A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol is Google's open standard for agent interoperability. As a Capability Operating System, supporting A2A enables our system to act as both an A2A server (exposing capabilities as agent skills) and A2A client (consuming external agents).

## Classification Guide

- **CORE**: A2A protocol types, agent cards, basic task management — needed for agent interop
- **EXTENDED**: Skills registry, agent profiles, advanced task management
- **ECOSYSTEM**: Agent marketplace, ratings/reviews

---

# Feature Catalog: Gap — Workflow Orchestration

> **Series**: 2300
> **EPICs**: EPIC-2300 (Workflow Engine), EPIC-2310 (Hooks System), EPIC-2320 (Payload Rules)
> **Gap Source**: diegosouza-omniroute (workflow FSM, payload rules, config hot-reload), cybernetics-core (hooks system, workflow registry, DAG orchestrator)
> **Total Features**: 30

## Gap Analysis Summary

Our catalog defines `KindWorkflow` capability type (129, P2) and references composite workflow capabilities, but lacks any actual workflow or orchestration implementation. The reference repos provide:

- **Workflow FSM** (diegosouza) — multi-step workflow state machine for complex request pipelines
- **Hooks System** (cybernetics-core) — registry of hooks with condition evaluation, BullMQ processing, and execution history
- **Workflow Registry** (cybernetics-core) — YAML workflow definitions, DAG orchestrator, retry policies
- **Payload Rules** (diegosouza) — hot-reloadable JSON rules per model/protocol for request/response transformation

These enable building complex multi-step workflows where a single request triggers a chain of LLM calls, tool executions, conditional branches, and data transformations.

## Classification Guide

- **CORE**: Hooks system (pre/post request hooks), payload rules — essential for request customization
- **EXTENDED**: Workflow engine, DAG orchestrator — valuable for complex pipelines
- **ECOSYSTEM**: Workflow marketplace, visual workflow editor

# Feature Catalog: Gap — MCP Governance

> **Series**: 2400
> **EPICs**: EPIC-2400 (Tool Risk Classification), EPIC-2410 (Value-Moving Gate), EPIC-2420 (Tool Design & Quality)
> **Gap Source**: cybernetics-core (tool governance, risk-level classification, family-based risk mapping, value-moving tool action gate, MCP tool design rubric)
> **Total Features**: 25

## Gap Analysis Summary

Our catalog has comprehensive MCP support (Series 900) covering protocol, transports, catalog, sandbox, and execution. However, we lack governance features specific to tool safety and risk classification from the cybernetics-core reference:

- **Tool risk classification** — classifying tools by risk level (low/medium/high/critical) based on their capabilities
- **Family-based risk mapping** — grouping tools into families with inherited risk levels
- **Value-moving tool action gate** — special policy gate for tools that move value (payments, transfers, trades)
- **Tool design rubric** — automated quality assessment for tool definitions (schema quality, naming, descriptions)
- **Runtime provider leases** — time-scoped, permission-bounded credentials for external runtimes

These features are critical for a Capability Operating System where tools can take real-world actions with financial or security implications.

## Classification Guide

- **CORE**: Tool risk classification, value-moving gate — critical for safe tool execution
- **EXTENDED**: Tool design rubric, runtime leases — quality and security enhancements
- **ECOSYSTEM**: Tool quality marketplace, automated rubric scoring

---

## Features

### Tool Risk Classification (2400-2409)

| # | Name | Description | Classification | Priority | Proposed EPIC |
|---|------|-------------|---------------|----------|---------------|
| 2400 | Tool Risk Level Model | Define `ToolRiskLevel` enum: `low` (read-only, informational), `medium` (state-changing, reversible), `high` (state-changing, irreversible), `critical` (value-moving, security-sensitive) | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2400 (new) |
| 2401 | Tool Risk Classifier | Implement tool risk classifier: analyze tool schema, name, description to auto-assign risk level; support manual override | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2400 |
| 2402 | Risk Classification Rules | Define risk classification rules: `read`/`list`/`get`/`search` → low, `create`/`update` → medium, `delete`/`execute`/`run` → high, `pay`/`transfer`/`trade` → critical | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2400 |
| 2403 | Tool Family Registry | Define tool families: group related tools (filesystem, network, database, financial, communication), assign family-level default risk | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2400 |
| 2404 | Family-Based Risk Inheritance | Inherit risk level from tool family: tools in `financial` family default to `critical`, tools in `filesystem.read` family default to `low` | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2400 |
| 2405 | Risk-Based Policy Integration | Integrate tool risk with policy engine: policies can reference risk level as condition; e.g., "deny all critical tools for viewer role" | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2400 |
| 2406 | Risk Level Admin Config | Admin endpoints for risk configuration: override auto-classified risk per tool, configure family risk defaults, view risk report | CORE | P1 | EPIC-2400 |

# Feature Catalog: Gap — Import/Export, Bootstrap & Operational

> **Series**: 2500
> **EPICs**: EPIC-2500 (Config Import/Export), EPIC-2510 (Bootstrap Service), EPIC-2520 (Operational Enhancements), EPIC-2530 (Compliance & No-Log)
> **Gap Source**: diegosouza-omniroute (pricing sync, config hot-reload, quota sharing, volume detector, heap pressure shedding, no-log keys, provider plans, credit balance), cybernetics-core (bootstrap service, config import/export, debug exposure gate, docker hostname transform, OAuth authorization server)
> **Total Features**: 35

## Gap Analysis Summary

Our catalog has CLI import/export (1137, 1138), seed data loading (11E0-11E2), and config loading (110-119). However, we lack several operational features from both reference repos:

- **Config import/export with validation** — preflight validation, redacted secret export, cross-environment promotion
- **Bootstrap service** — automated first-run setup from environment
- **Volume detection & load shedding** — request spike detection, automatic load shedding
- **Quota sharing** — pool quotas across multiple keys/groups
- **Compliance/no-log keys** — GDPR-compliant operation mode
- **Debug exposure gate** — controlled debug info exposure
- **OAuth authorization server** — full RFC-compliant OAuth server (not just client)
- **Docker hostname transforms** — localhost → host.docker.internal in containers

## Classification Guide

- **CORE**: Config import/export, bootstrap, load shedding, no-log keys — operational necessities
- **EXTENDED**: Quota sharing, debug gate, OAuth server, volume detection
- **ECOSYSTEM**: Docker transforms, pricing sync UI

# 0010 — Warp-Prism Foundation Audit Analyzer Baseline

> **Audit Date**: 2026-06-07
> **Auditor**: Hermes Agent (Task 0010 execution)
> **Scope**: Full lib/ tree inventory, missing file detection, naming/API verification, command baseline
> **Method**: Direct source file reads + filesystem inspection; Flutter SDK check

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The Warp-Prism project is a Flutter application (`pubspec.yaml` declares Flutter SDK, `go_router`, `flutter_riverpod`, etc.) with a substantial design system layer (40 Dart files in `lib/`) but **no application entrypoint**. The project cannot compile, analyze, or test because:

1. **`lib/main.dart`** does not exist (no Flutter entrypoint)
2. **`lib/app/app.dart`** does not exist (no app root widget)
3. **`lib/app/router.dart`** does not exist (no routing configuration)
4. **`test/` directory** does not exist (no tests at all)
5. **Flutter SDK** is not installed in the execution environment
6. **README.md** is still Next.js/v0 boilerplate

**Critical finding**: The naming/API mismatches reported in `docs/draft.md` and `EPIC-00` (DsShell vs DSShell, DsColors vs DSColors, body: vs content:) **do NOT exist in the current codebase**. All 40 Dart files consistently use `DS*` (uppercase prefix) naming. The `draft.md` analysis appears to have been based on an earlier version of the code or contained errors.

---

## 7. Potential Compile Issues (Source Inspection Only)

return AnimatedBuilder(

`AnimatedBuilder` is **not a standard Flutter class**. The correct class is `AnimatedBuilder` (which IS valid in Flutter 3.10+). This should work with the declared SDK `>=3.0.0 <4.0.0` but may need verification.

### 7.2 `ds_glow_border.dart` line 126
```dart
return AnimatedBuilder(
```
Same as above — uses `AnimatedBuilder` which is a valid Flutter widget.

```dart
final (icon, color) = switch (trend) {
  DSTrend.up => (Icons.trending_up, DSColors.statusSuccess),
  ...
};
```
Uses Dart 3 pattern matching / switch expressions. Requires Dart 3.0+ (declared in pubspec: `sdk: '>=3.0.0 <4.0.0'`). Should work.

# 0310 — Backbone Model Contract Audit Report

> **Audit Date**: 2026-06-07
> **Auditor**: Hermes Agent (Task 0310 execution)
> **Scope**: Data model backbone contract — current vs required
> **Method**: Direct source reads of models.dart, workspace_parser.dart, prompt.txt, research.md, mock-workspace-corpus-contract.md

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The current `models.dart` (598 lines) defines a generic `Asset`/`AssetType`/`AssetEdge` contract that covers only 5 of the 9 required asset kinds, uses freeform strings for edge types, omits canonicality entirely, and bakes pipeline-oriented metadata (SkillInput/SkillOutput/SkillStep, WorkflowTrigger/WorkflowStage/RetryPolicy) into classes that should instead carry frontmatter data. The normalized backbone contract has been defined and implemented across 4 new files totaling ~220 lines of focused Dart, with a barrel export and comprehensive tests.

---

## 2. Current State Audit

### 2.1 AssetType (current) vs AssetKind (required)

| Current AssetType | Required AssetKind | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `agent` | `agent` | ✅ Present |
| `skill` | `skill` | ✅ Present |
| — | `subskill` | ❌ MISSING |
| `workflow` | `workflow` | ✅ Present |
| `task` | `task` | ✅ Present |
| `doc` | — | ⚠️ Not in required contract; replaced by specific kinds |
| — | `changelog` | ❌ MISSING |
| — | `script` | ❌ MISSING |
| — | `reference` | ❌ MISSING |
| — | `rule` | ❌ MISSING |

**Gap**: 4 of 9 required kinds are missing. The `doc` value has no direct equivalent in the prompt contract.

### 2.2 Edge Type

| Aspect | Current | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Type | `String edgeType` (freeform) | `EdgeKind` enum (7 values) |
| Values | `"uses"`, `"triggers"`, `"references"`, `"delegates"` (comment only) | `contains`, `routesTo`, `dependsOn`, `references`, `changedBy`, `proves`, `uses` |

**Gap**: No typed enum. Freeform strings invite inconsistency.

### 2.3 Canonicality

| Aspect | Current | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Exists? | No | Yes — 6 values |
| Values | — | `parentCanonical`, `childLocal`, `generated`, `appendOnly`, `archive`, `mock` |

**Gap**: Completely absent. The research.md and prompt.txt both require provenance classification.

### 2.4 Base Class

| Aspect | Current (Asset) | Required (WorkspaceAsset) |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `kind` | Via `assetType` getter | `AssetKind kind` |
| `name` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `path` | ❌ Missing | ✅ Required |
| `description` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `canonicality` | ❌ Missing | ✅ Required |
| `frontmatter` | ❌ (uses `metadata: Map`) | ✅ Required |
| `tags` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `triggers` | ❌ Missing | ✅ Required |
| `edges` | ❌ Missing (separate `AssetEdge` list) | ✅ Inline |
| `version` | ✅ | ❌ Not in target contract |
| `createdAt/updatedAt` | ✅ | ❌ Not in target (dates in frontmatter) |

**Gap**: `path`, `canonicality`, `frontmatter`, `triggers`, `edges` missing from current. `version`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` are not in the target contract (they live in frontmatter).

### 2.5 Specialized Classes

| Current Class | Target Approach | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| `Agent` (status, model, systemPrompt, capabilities, tools, skillIds, workflowIds) | Flat frontmatter: name, model (string), mode, description, skills, workflows | Current is over-structured; target is simpler frontmatter |
| `AgentModel` (provider, name, temperature, maxTokens) | Replaced by `model: "provider/name"` string | Remove |
| `AgentTool`, `ToolParameter` | Not in target contract | Remove |
| `Skill` (inputs, outputs, steps, usedByAgentIds) | Frontmatter: name, description, triggers, sub_skills, canonicality, tags | Current is pipeline-oriented; target is frontmatter-oriented |
| `SkillInput`, `SkillOutput`, `SkillStep` | Not in target contract | Remove |
| `Workflow` (trigger, stages, errorHandling, avgDuration, successRate) | Frontmatter: name, description, uses_skills, kind | Current is pipeline-oriented; target is simpler |
| `WorkflowTrigger`, `WorkflowStage`, `WorkflowErrorHandling`, `RetryPolicy`, `FallbackRule` | Not in target contract | Remove |
| `Task` (status, priority, assignedAgentId, workflowId, startedAt, completedAt, progress) | Frontmatter: id, title, status, priority, owner, created, updated, skills, workflows, depends_on, proof_state, review_score | Different field set |
| `ChangelogEntry` (summary, changes, affectedAssets, evidence, author) | Frontmatter: id, date, project, task, type, impact, skills; body: Why/Changed/Evidence | Completely different structure |
| `AssetEdge` (sourceId, targetId, edgeType: String) | `WorkspaceEdge` (sourceId, targetId, kind: EdgeKind, metadata) | Superseded by typed edge |

### 2.6 Parser (workspace_parser.dart)

| Parser | Current | Target |
|---|---|---|
| `parseAgent` | Parses full YAML (AgentModel, tools, capabilities) | Parse frontmatter from .md |
| `parseSkill` | Parses full YAML (inputs, outputs, steps) | Parse frontmatter from .md |
| `parseWorkflow` | Parses full YAML (trigger, stages, errorHandling) | Parse frontmatter from .md |
| `parseTask` | Does not exist | New parser needed |
| `parseChangelog` | Heading-based markdown parsing | Frontmatter extraction |
| `parseFrontmatter` | Does not exist | New utility needed |
| Graph normalizer | Does not exist | New: build WorkspaceEdge list from cross-references |

---

## 3. Normalized Backbone Implemented

### 3.1 New Files Created

| File | Purpose | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/data/models/workspace_graph.dart` | AssetKind, EdgeKind, Canonicality, WorkspaceAsset, WorkspaceEdge | ~160 |
| `lib/data/models/task_contracts.dart` | TaskLane, ProofState, TaskMetadata, parsing extensions | ~150 |
| `lib/data/models/changelog_contracts.dart` | ChangelogType, ChangelogMetadata, parsing extension | ~100 |
| `lib/data/models/governance_diagnostics.dart` | DiagnosticSeverity, DiagnosticCategory, GovernanceDiagnostic | ~110 |
| `lib/data/models/data_models.dart` | Barrel export for all backbone files | ~15 |
| `test/data/models/workspace_graph_models_test.dart` | Comprehensive backbone contract tests | ~280 |

### 3.2 Existing Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/data/models/models.dart` | Added SUPERSEDED notice in doc comment; file retained for backward compatibility with workspace_parser.dart |

### 3.3 Decision: Legacy Retention

The legacy `models.dart` is **retained but superseded**. It is the only file imported by `workspace_parser.dart`, which is the only consumer. Removing it would break the existing parser immediately. The new backbone is the canonical contract; downstream tasks (0311-0315) will migrate the parser and any other consumers to the new types, at which point `models.dart` can be archived.

---

## 4. Validation Commands

| Command | Expected Result | Actual Result |
|---|---|---|
| `flutter analyze lib/data/models` | 0 errors | **BLOCKED**: Flutter SDK not installed |
| `flutter test test/data/models/workspace_graph_models_test.dart` | 0 failures | **BLOCKED**: Flutter SDK not installed |
| `dart analyze lib/data/models` | 0 errors | **BLOCKED**: Dart SDK not standalone |

**Blocker**: Flutter SDK is not installed in the execution environment. All static analysis and test execution commands are blocked. The models are syntactically valid Dart based on manual inspection.

---

## 5. Downstream Impact

| Task | Impact |
|---|---|
| Task 0311 (Parser rewrite) | Can now target `WorkspaceAsset`, `TaskMetadata`, `ChangelogMetadata` types |
| Task 0312 (Repository) | Can now build repositories returning `WorkspaceAsset` lists |
| Task 0313 (Graph normalization) | Can now use `WorkspaceEdge` with typed `EdgeKind` |
| Task 0314 (Diagnostics service) | Can now produce `GovernanceDiagnostic` payloads |
| Task 0315 (Provider contracts) | Can now consume all backbone types in Riverpod providers |

---

## 6. Key Design Decisions

1. **WorkspaceAsset carries raw frontmatter**: Rather than duplicating every frontmatter field as a Dart property, `WorkspaceAsset.frontmatter` holds the raw map. Kind-specific metadata (TaskMetadata, ChangelogMetadata) is extracted by parsers and stored alongside. This keeps the backbone lean while supporting typed access.

2. **Equality is shallow**: WorkspaceAsset and WorkspaceEdge equality is based on identity fields (id, kind, name, path for assets; sourceId, targetId, kind for edges), not deep frontmatter comparison. This supports efficient graph operations.

3. **Parsing extensions live with their types**: `TaskLaneParsing`, `ProofStateParsing`, `ChangelogTypeParsing`, and `DiagnosticSeverityParsing` are extension methods co-located with their enums. This keeps parsing logic discoverable without polluting the enum definitions.

4. **GovernanceDiagnostic is asset-scoped**: Each diagnostic entry references exactly one `assetId`. Multi-asset diagnostics (e.g., broken edges) use the source asset id. This simplifies the UI grouping model.

---

## CRITICAL Gaps (Block CyberCore operational viability)

### GAP-C1: Data Table Component — MISSING
Sortable, filterable, column-configurable, paginated table with operational state cell renderers, virtual scrolling, glass-panel styling. Needed for: MCP server registry (1400+ rows), agents, skills, tasks, capabilities, providers, policies, users, audit events, credentials.

### GAP-C2: Command Palette / Global Search — MISSING
`Cmd+K` keyboard-driven command palette with fuzzy search, category grouping (navigate/run/recent), overlay positioning, action execution. Primary navigation interface for power users.

### GAP-C3: Log/Event Streaming Viewer — MISSING
Severity levels, source filtering, text search, auto-scroll, virtualized rendering for 10K+ entries. Different from `DSTimeline` (structured metadata) — this is streaming log with severity/source/text.

---

## IMPORTANT Gaps (Degrade operational quality)

### GAP-I1: Graph Visualization Maturity — PARTIAL
Current `DSGraphCanvas` is a 483-line monolith. Missing: hierarchical/tree layout, layered DAG layout, radial layout, graph filtering, minimap, node hover preview, accessibility, edge differentiation, composability.

### GAP-I2: Loading Skeleton — MISSING
No shimmer/skeleton placeholder. `DSStateSurface.loading` shows only a spinner. Need content-shaped skeletons for cards, table rows, graph nodes.

### GAP-I3: Notification/Toast System — MISSING
Rule says notifier owns snackbar, but NO reusable snackbar/toast widget exists. Need severity coloring, stacking, auto-dismiss, action buttons, Riverpod integration.

### GAP-I4: Health Dashboard — PARTIAL
`DSStatusDot` + `DSMetricTile` exist. Missing: compound health cards, status grid/matrix, sparkline/trend mini-charts, uptime bars.

### GAP-I5: Operational State Vocabulary — PARTIAL
`DSStateType` has 3 states (empty, loading, error). Need 14+: healthy, degraded, error, disabled, pending, running, approved, rejected, redacted, exposed, stale, unverified, promoted, archived.

### GAP-I6: Error Boundary — MISSING
No `DSErrorBoundary`. One panel crash kills entire app. Need `ErrorWidget.builder` override, fallback UI, isolation, retry mechanism.

### GAP-I7: Drag-and-Drop — MISSING
`DSLaneBoard` has no drag-and-drop. `DSDraggableCard`, `DSDropTarget`, `DSReorderableLane` needed for task board interactivity.

FILE: reports/epic-10-glass-performance-budget.md

# EPIC 10 — Glass Performance Budget

> **Generated**: 2026-06-07 by Task 1040
> **Scope**: Blur, BackdropFilter, and glass panel usage audit
> **Method**: Full-text search for `DSGlassPanel`, `DSGlassPanelSimple`, `BackdropFilter`, and `blur` in `lib/`

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The Warp-Prism design system is **already well-aligned** with the research brief's "sparse glassmorphism" guidance. Of 40 design-system files, only **one host** uses the expensive `DSGlassPanel` (with BackdropFilter blur): `DSStoryPanel`. All other surfaces use `DSGlassPanelSimple` (solid color, no blur) or plain `Container` with `BoxDecoration`.

No surgical swaps are needed. This report codifies the current state as a **policy** so future work does not reintroduce gratuitous blur.

---

## 2. Budget Policy

### 2.1 Surface Classification

| Category | Panel Type | Blur Level | Where Allowed |
|----------|-----------|------------|---------------|
| **Narrative / Story** | `DSGlassPanel.elevated` | sigma 15 | `DSStoryPanel` — low-count, high-value insight surface |
| **Detail / Inspector** | `DSGlassPanelSimple` | none | `DSDetailInspector`, `DSPropertyRow` — dense data, no blur benefit |
| **Cards / Lists** | `DSGlassPanelSimple` or plain `Container` | none | `DSAssetCard`, `DSTaskCard`, `DSMetricTile`, `DSStoryCardQuick` — high-frequency surfaces |
| **Board / Lanes** | plain `Container` | none | `DSLaneBoard`, `_LaneColumn` — horizontal scroll, many items |
| **Graph / Canvas** | plain `Container` | none | `DSGraphCanvas` — 60fps physics, no blur overhead |
| **Shell / Navigation** | plain `Container` | none | `DSShell`, `DSSidebar`, `DSTopbar` — always-visible, must be fast |
| **Modals / Overlays** | `DSGlassPanel.modal` | sigma 20 | Reserved for future modal dialogs — justified by single-instance usage |

### 2.2 Rules

1. **Default is simple.** New surfaces MUST use `DSGlassPanelSimple` or plain `Container` unless explicitly justified.
2. **Blur requires justification.** Any new `DSGlassPanel` usage must be documented in this budget with a reason.
3. **No blur nesting.** Never place a `DSGlassPanel` inside another `DSGlassPanel`. The `ClipRRect` + `BackdropFilter` stack compounds GPU cost.
4. **No blur on scrollable lists.** `ListView.builder`, `GridView.builder`, and horizontal `SingleChildScrollView` surfaces MUST NOT contain `BackdropFilter` children.
5. **High-frequency = simple.** Any surface rendered once-per-item in a list (cards, markers, chips) must use the simple path.
6. **Modal blur is acceptable.** `DSGlassPanel.modal` (sigma 20) is reserved for true modals/overlays where only one instance is visible at a time.

### 2.3 Blur Inventory (current)

| Host | Panel Used | Blur Sigma | Justification | Status |
|------|-----------|------------|---------------|--------|
| `DSStoryPanel` | `DSGlassPanel.elevated` | 15 | Primary narrative insight surface. Low count (1-3 per screen). High visual value for "observatory" feel. | **KEEP** |
| `DSStoryCardQuick` | `DSGlassPanelSimple` | 0 | Dashboard metric tiles — high frequency | ✅ Already simple |
| `DSMetricTile` | `DSGlassPanelSimple` | 0 | Metric display — high frequency | ✅ Already simple |
| `DSAssetCard` | plain `Container` | 0 | List cards — high frequency | ✅ No glass |
| `DSTaskCard` | plain `Container` | 0 | Lane cards — high frequency, scrollable | ✅ No glass |
| `DSLaneBoard` | plain `Container` | 0 | Board columns — horizontal scroll | ✅ No glass |
| `DSGraphCanvas` | plain `Container` | 0 | Physics canvas — 60fps target | ✅ No glass |
| `DSDetailInspector` | plain `Container` | 0 | Detail sections — dense data | ✅ No glass |
| `DSShell` | plain `Container` | 0 | App shell — always visible | ✅ No glass |
| `DSSidebar` | plain `Container` | 0 | Navigation — always visible | ✅ No glass |
| `DSTopbar` | plain `Container` | 0 | Search/actions — always visible | ✅ No glass |

**Total BackdropFilter instances in hosts: 1** (DSStoryPanel only)

### 2.4 Glass Panel Tier Reference

| Constructor | Blur Sigma | Shadows | Intended Use |
|-------------|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `DSGlassPanel.subtle` | 5 | none | Hover emphasis, subtle elevation |
| `DSGlassPanel` (default) | 10 | none | General-purpose (use sparingly) |
| `DSGlassPanel.elevated` | 15 | elevation2 | Story panels, hero surfaces |
| `DSGlassPanel.modal` | 20 | elevation4 | Modal overlays (single instance) |
| `DSGlassPanelSimple` | 0 | configurable | Default for all other surfaces |

---

## 3. Performance Notes

### 3.1 BackdropFilter Cost Model

`BackdropFilter` with `ImageFilter.blur()` requires Flutter to rasterize the area behind the widget and apply a Gaussian blur shader. The cost scales with:
- **Area**: Larger blur regions cost more.
- **Sigma**: Higher blur radius requires more texture samples.
- **Nesting**: Nested `BackdropFilter` widgets multiply the rasterization cost.

On desktop (the primary target), a single `BackdropFilter` with sigma 15 on a ~400x600px story panel is well within budget. The risk arises only if blur surfaces proliferate into lists or boards.

### 3.2 Current Risk Assessment

**Risk: LOW.** The codebase has exactly one BackdropFilter host. No further optimization is needed.

### 3.3 GlowBorder Animation

`DSGlowBorder` uses `AnimationController` with continuous animation. This is acceptable for 1-3 instances but should not be used on every card in a list. Current usage is limited to decorative borders on selected/hovered items.

---

## 4. Enforcement

The regression test `test/design_system/glass_budget_test.dart` verifies:
- `DSStoryPanel` uses `DSGlassPanel.elevated` (blur justifiied)
- `DSStoryCardQuick` uses `DSGlassPanelSimple` (no blur)
- `DSMetricTile` uses `DSGlassPanelSimple` (no blur)
- The `DSGlassPanel` class documents its sparse-usage contract

---

## 5. Recommendations for Future Work

1. **If adding a new host**: Start with `DSGlassPanelSimple`. Only upgrade to `DSGlassPanel` if the surface meets all criteria: low count (<5 per screen), non-scrollable, high visual value.
2. **Gallery/demo page**: When the demo gallery is built, it should include a glass budget section showing which surfaces use blur and why.
3. **Profiling**: Once a runnable app exists, use Flutter DevTools to verify BackdropFilter cost on the story panel. If GPU frame time exceeds 8ms on the target hardware, consider reducing the blur to `DSGlassPanel.subtle` (sigma 5).

| Surface | Widget | Focus Support | Semantics | Keyboard Activation |
|---------|--------|--------------|-----------|-------------------|
| Sidebar item | `_SidebarItemWidget` in `ds_sidebar.dart` | MouseRegion only | None | None (GestureDetector only) |
| Topbar action | `DSTopbarAction` in `ds_topbar.dart` | MouseRegion only | None | None |
| Task card | `DSTaskCard` in `ds_task_card.dart` | Not audited | Not audited | Not audited |
| Lane board | `DSLaneBoard` | No focus traversal | None | None |
| Timeline entry | `DSTimelineMarker` in `ds_timeline_marker.dart` | Not audited | Not audited | Not audited |
| Filter chips | `DSFilterChipGroup` in `ds_filter_chip_group.dart` | Not audited | Not audited | Not audited |
| Search bar | `DSSearchBar` in `ds_search_bar.dart` | Likely has (TextField) | Likely has | Likely has |

### 5.2 Responsive Breakpoints

All breakpoints are **hardcoded literals**, not centralized tokens:

- `DSShellResponsive.breakpoint`: 1200.0 (constructor param, default)
- `_MasterDetailTemplateState.build`: `> 1200` (wide), `> 800` (medium)
- `TimelineTemplate.build`: `> 1000` (wide)
- `DSShellResponsive.build`: `>= 800` (showFullSidebar)

**Gap**: No `DSBreakpoints` token class. No narrow breakpoint (<600px). No orientation-independent layout switching.

### 5.3 State Rendering Inventory

| State Type | Widgets That Handle It | Widgets That Don't |
|------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| Empty | `_EmptyLane` (ds_lane_board), `_EmptyTimeline` (ds_timeline) | Graph canvas, detail inspector, story panel, search results, filter results |
| Loading | None | Everything |
| Error | None | Everything |
| Skeleton/Shimmer | None | Everything |

### 5.4 Blur / Glass Usage

| Widget | Blur Level | Has Fallback? | Usage Context |
|--------|-----------|---------------|---------------|
| `DSGlassPanel` (default) | sigma 10 | `DSGlassPanelSimple` exists | General panels |
| `DSGlassPanel.subtle` | sigma 5 | Via Simple fallback | Subtle cards |
| `DSGlassPanel.elevated` | sigma 15 | Via Simple fallback | Story panels, elevated cards |
| `DSGlassPanel.modal` | sigma 20 | Via Simple fallback | Modal overlays |
| Canvas overlay in `CanvasTemplate` | withOpacity(0.95), no blur | None | Graph inspector overlay |

**Note**: `DSGlassPanelSimple` exists as a no-blur performance alternative. Research.md recommends "sparse glassmorphism" — the current tiered approach (5/10/15/20) is reasonable but must not be stacked.

### 5.5 Demo Narrative Surfaces

## 9. Blockers for EPIC 10

1. **No main.dart / app shell**: EPIC 10 polish requires screens to polish. No `main.dart`, `app.dart`, `router.dart`, or any page exists.
2. **No Flutter SDK on audit machine**: Cannot validate with `flutter analyze` or `flutter test`.
3. **No test files**: Zero `*_test.dart` files in the project. Regression testing is impossible.
4. **README is stale**: Still describes Next.js/v0 project. Would misroute any contributor.
5. **Model gaps**: `AssetType` has 5 values vs 9 needed; no `Canonicality` enum; no `EdgeKind` enum.
6. **Mock data format**: Existing mocks are `.yaml` pure, not `.md` with YAML frontmatter as required by prompt.
7. **API mismatches documented in draft.md**: Template-to-organism API inconsistencies (DsColors vs DSColors, DsMotion vs DSMotion, parameter name mismatches) — these may or may not have been fixed since the draft was written.

---

## 10. What Can Be Polished Now vs What Is Blocked

### Can proceed (design system widget-level polish):
- Contrast ratio fixes in `ds_colors.dart` (textTertiary)
- Focus traversal additions to interactive atoms/molecules/organisms
- Semantics wrappers on all components
- Breakpoint centralization into a token class
- Loading/error state widget creation
- Glass panel tier validation and documentation
- Centralized responsive breakpoint tokens

### Blocked (needs app surfaces first):
- End-to-end keyboard navigation testing
- Screen-level responsive behavior
- Demo narrative path / gallery page
- Storytelling copy for Map/Operate/History/Governance
- Performance profiling on real screens
- Loading/error states on actual data flows
- Empty state behavior in context (graph, search, detail)

## 11. Operational Recommendations

1. **Immediate**: Replace `README.md` with Flutter project documentation.
2. **Before EPIC 10 tasks**: Create `main.dart` + app shell + router so polish can be visually verified.
3. **During Task 1010**: Fix `textTertiary` contrast (raise to at least #808090 for WCAG AA on #050508).
4. **During Task 1020**: Create `DSBreakpoints` token class. Centralize all breakpoint values.
5. **During Task 1030**: Create reusable loading skeleton and error panel atoms.
6. **Model alignment**: Rename `AssetType` → `AssetKind`, add missing values, add `Canonicality` and `EdgeKind` enums before data layer work.

1. **App deve compilar antes de UI**: Tasks 0010→0011→0012 devem completar antes de qualquer
   tela de produto. O `flutter analyze` deve passar (ou residual documentado) antes de 0017+.

2. **Design system antes de telas**: Tasks 0014→0015→0016→0017 devem preceder Map/Operate/
   History/Governance.

3. **Mock corpus antes de data layer**: Tasks 0001→0006 devem existir antes que 0311/0312
   possam funcionar com dados reais.

4. **Quick wins 0019/0020**: Podem ser executadas após 0011+0017, independentemente do
   EPIC 03 completo. São "workspace snapshot" que escaneiam diretório real.

5. **Tasks 0310-0315 são o backbone**: Sem elas, nenhuma tela de produto pode consumir
   dados normalizados. São a maior dependência transversal.

6. **EPIC 10 (1000-1060)**: Executável em paralelo com tudo porque depende apenas de 1000
   (Onda 0). Mas 1060 (audit final) precisa de 1010-1050 completos.

7. **Ordem dentro de cada onda**: Tasks marcadas [S] no mesmo domínio devem ser sequenciadas.
   Tasks [P] em domínios diferentes podem correr em paralelo por agentes independentes.

# Flutter Reference Repo Sweep — Architectural Patterns Report

> **Date**: 2026-06-08
> **Author**: architects (subagent)
> **Scope**: 37 archived Flutter/Dart repos in `.archive/flutter-reference-repos-20260608/`
> **Purpose**: Extract frontend component patterns not yet captured in flutter-harness or task tree

---

## Top Reference Repos

| # | Repo | Architectural Value |
|---|------|-------------------|
| 1 | `dart_agent_core` | **Critical** — full Dart-native agent framework with streaming, eval, skills, controller hooks |
| 2 | `skill_tree` | **High** — custom RenderObject graph/tree/DAG visualization |
| 3 | `achieve-flutter-architecture` | **High** — production fintech architecture (6yr, 30+ features): DataPage lifecycle, caching, EventBus |
| 4 | `abhishek_doshi_portfolio` | **High** — responsive sections, animated stats, hover cards, values system |
| 5 | `flutter-binance-ui` | **Medium-High** — data-dense financial dashboard |
| 6 | `cocktails-demo` | **Medium** — parallax scroll, custom page transitions |
| 7 | `SkillSync-Flutter` | **Medium** — notification tiles, review cards, star rating, theme provider |
| 8 | `conalyz_cli` | **Medium** — Flutter accessibility static analysis tool (AST-based) |
| 9 | `agent-skills` | **Medium** — scenario→slice decomposition, session state, UI verification |
| 10 | `flutter-forge` | **Medium** — Mason templates + Clean Architecture + BDD testing |

---

## Critical Finding: `dart_agent_core`

The single most valuable repo. A **published Dart-native agent framework** (v1.0.13 on pub.dev) with:
- Full agentic loop with streaming, tool use, planning, skills, sub-agents
- Controller hooks for UI integration (approve/block tool calls, observe events)
- Typed streaming events: `modelChunkMessage`, `fullModelMessage`, `functionCallRequest`, `functionCallResult`, `modelRetrying`
- PlanState model: `PlanStep` with statuses (pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled)
- Dynamic skill toggle (forceActivate vs optional)
- Loop detector with confidence scoring
- EpisodicMemory with context compression
- Complete eval framework (EvalRunner, trials, graders, pass@k, transcript recording)

**Should be treated as primary reference architecture for Warp Prism agent runtime integration.**

---

## 2. Canonical Naming Convention

**Standard**: All design system classes use `DS` prefix (uppercase S).

| Layer | Convention | Examples |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| Tokens | `DS{Domain}` | `DSColors`, `DSTypography`, `DSSpacing`, `DSRadii`, `DSShadows`, `DSMotion`, `DSSemantics` |
| Atoms | `DS{Component}` | `DSText`, `DSIcon`, `DSBadge`, `DSChip`, `DSStatusDot`, `DSDivider`, `DSGlowBorder`, `DSGlassPanel` |
| Molecules | `DS{Component}` | `DSSearchBar`, `DSFilterChipGroup`, `DSAssetCard`, `DSMetricTile`, `DSProvenancePill`, `DSTaskCard`, `DSEvidenceRow`, `DSTimelineMarker` |
| Organisms | `DS{Component}` | `DSShell`, `DSSidebar`, `DSTopbar`, `DSLaneBoard`, `DSTimeline`, `DSDetailInspector`, `DSStoryPanel`, `DSGraphCanvas` |
| Templates | `{Name}Template` | `MasterDetailTemplate`, `CanvasTemplate`, `TimelineTemplate` |
| Enums | `DS{Domain}{Variant}` | `DSTextVariant`, `DSIconSize`, `DSBadgeSize`, `DSChipSize`, `DSTrend` |
| Data classes | `DS{Domain}` | `DSSidebarItem`, `DSTimelineEntry`, `DSLane`, `DSLaneTask`, `DSFilterOption`, etc. |

**Verification**: `grep -r 'Ds[A-Z]' lib/design_system/` returns 0 matches. All 38 files use `DS*` consistently.

| **Inter font not declared** | 🟡 Medium | `pubspec.yaml` + `ds_typography.dart` | `DSTypography.fontFamilySans = 'Inter'` but pubspec only declares `JetBrainsMono`. Inter will fall back to system sans-serif. |
| **No `main.dart` entrypoint** | 🔴 Critical | `lib/main.dart` | Flutter app entrypoint missing — prevents compilation |

### 9.3 Font Contract Decision

The `DSTypography` class references two font families:
- `JetBrainsMono` — ✅ Declared in pubspec.yaml (Regular, Medium/Bold weights)
- `Inter` — ⚠️ NOT declared in pubspec.yaml

**Resolution options** (to be decided in a future task):
1. Add Inter font to `assets/fonts/` and declare in pubspec.yaml
2. Replace `Inter` with `JetBrainsMono` for sans-serif usage (monospace-first design)
3. Use system sans-serif as fallback (current behavior — implicit)

## Overlaps Found and Disposition

### 1. App bootstrap overlap: `Task 0011`, `Task 0017`, `Task 0410`

**Problem**: Three tasks referenced creation of `lib/main.dart`, `lib/app/app.dart`, and `lib/app/router.dart`.

**Resolution applied**:

- `Task 0011` remains the owner of the minimum Flutter bootstrap.
- `Task 0017` now consumes `Task 0011` and only adds Design System Gallery route/page wiring.
- `Task 0410` now consumes `Task 0011` and expands product route skeletons for Overview/Map/Operate/History/Governance/Asset Detail.

**Residual risk**: Builders must execute `0011` before `0017` or `0410`; otherwise they may recreate bootstrap work from stale mental context.

### 2. Changelog corpus overlap: `Task 0005` and `Task 0710`

**Problem**: Both tasks attempted to create 12+ changelog markdown entries.

**Resolution applied**:

- `Task 0005` remains owner of the base EPIC-02 changelog corpus.
- `Task 0710` now enriches/verifies that base corpus for History-specific filters, story grouping, and multi-hop impact paths.

**Residual risk**: If `0710` runs before `0005`, it is blocked by missing base corpus; this is now explicit via `Depends on: Task 0005`.

### 3. Governance diagnostics overlap: `Task 0314` and `0810`-`0813`

**Problem**: Both the data-layer epic and Governance screen epic mention diagnostics.

**Disposition**: This is a healthy layer split, not a blocker.

- `Task 0314` owns computation/service contracts.
- `Task 0810`-`0813` own UI panels, analytics presentation, and drill-down storytelling.

Builders should treat `0314` as a strict dependency for Governance UI work.

### 4. Universal detail vs feature-specific inspectors

**Problem**: Map and Operate tasks include inspector/detail behavior, while EPIC-09 owns universal detail.

**Disposition**: Healthy phased split if constrained.

- `0513` and `0612` may provide feature-local summaries/inspectors.
- `0901`-`0905` own canonical universal detail route/view-model/responsive shell.
- Feature-specific inspector tasks must avoid inventing incompatible asset IDs or independent detail descriptor models.

## Gaps / Watch Items

No prompt-critical missing epic was found. Remaining gaps are sequencing or proof risks:

1. **No single builder execution sequence file exists yet.**  
   The task graph is inferable, but builders will benefit from a short execution-order guide. This report supplies the recommended sequence below; create a dedicated workflow/guide only if this becomes recurring.

2. **Task 1070 is still open despite evidence filled.**  
   It can remain open as a gate, but if the project treats filled evidence as completion, a reviewer should later move it through normal review lanes. Do not use it as a reason to renumber again unless new collisions appear.

3. **Dependencies sometimes reference whole epics instead of exact task IDs.**  
   Examples include `EPIC 03 provider contract evidence` or `EPIC 04 shell baseline`. This is acceptable for planning readability, but builders should resolve these to concrete prerequisite tasks before execution. High-value mappings:
   - EPIC-03 provider contracts → `Task 0315`.

   - EPIC-03 diagnostics → `Task 0314`.
   - EPIC-04 shell baseline → `Task 0410`-`0413` depending on surface.

5. **Widgetbook is recommended in research but not explicitly tasked.**  
   This is not a prompt blocker. The current DS Gallery path is sufficient for the prototype. Widgetbook can remain a future enhancement unless the user explicitly wants a widget sandbox dependency.

6. **Controlled execution hooks from research phase 3 are intentionally absent.**

## Verification

Duplicate-ID audit command executed from repository root:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
root = Path('/home/sephiroth/working/ganthritor/warp-prism/docs/tasks/01-open')
rows = []
errors = []
for path in sorted(root.glob('*.md')):
    text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    header = re.search(r'^# Task (\d{4})\b', text, re.M)
    file_id = path.name.split('-', 1)[0]
    header_id = header.group(1) if header else None
    rows.append((file_id, header_id, path.name))
    if not header_id:
        errors.append(f'MISSING_HEADER {path.name}')
    elif file_id != header_id:
        errors.append(f'MISMATCH file={file_id} header={header_id} {path.name}')
from collections import defaultdict
by_file = defaultdict(list)
by_header = defaultdict(list)
for file_id, header_id, name in rows:
    by_file[file_id].append(name)
    if header_id:
        by_header[header_id].append(name)
file_dupes = {k:v for k,v in by_file.items() if len(v)>1}
header_dupes = {k:v for k,v in by_header.items() if len(v)>1}
print(f'total_files={len(rows)}')
print(f'unique_file_ids={len(by_file)}')
print(f'unique_header_ids={len(by_header)}')
print(f'file_duplicate_ids={file_dupes}')
print(f'header_duplicate_ids={header_dupes}')
print(f'mismatch_or_missing={errors}')
if file_dupes or header_dupes or errors:
    raise SystemExit(1)
PY
```

Result:

```text
total_files=55
unique_file_ids=55
unique_header_ids=55
file_duplicate_ids={}
header_duplicate_ids={}
mismatch_or_missing=[]
```

- No Flutter application source files were modified by this remediation.
- The remediation intentionally did not move tasks between lanes.
- The remediation corrected a false statement in Task 0010: `warp-prism/docs/draft.md` exists, but it is secondary planning evidence and must not replace fresh source and command evidence.

# EPIC-11 — Warp Prism Cybernetics Core Frontend

> **Planning Status**: Active Epic
> **Executable?**: No — planning artifact only.
> **Origin**: User clarified that Warp Prism must support a reusable operational ADS plus future Cybernetics Core frontend work, not just a mock ASW Observatory.
> **Depends on**: `1100-warp-prism-operational-atomic-design-system-epic.md`, Task 1101, Task 1102, Task 1103.

## Goal

Define the governed path from Warp Prism's reusable Flutter operational atomic design system to a Cybernetics Core frontend implementation. The first delivery target is not a destructive migration from the current Next.js frontend; it is an evidence-backed Flutter app/pilot inside the Warp Prism monorepo that can consume `warp_prism_ui`, mirror selected Cybernetics Core admin surfaces with fixed fixtures, and later decide whether to become a replacement, companion, or design-system reference implementation.

## Source Evidence

- `warp-prism/docs/tasks/00-planning/1100-warp-prism-operational-atomic-design-system-epic.md` defines Warp Prism as the ADS and catalog foundation for Cybernetics Core first.
- `warp-prism/docs/tasks/01-open/1102-warp-prism-control-surface-inventory.md` requires Cybernetics Core surface inventory and pilot matrix.
- Parent Cybernetics Core current frontend lives under `cyberneticscore/apps/frontend/` and backend/API under `cyberneticscore/apps/backend/`.
- Parent completed tasks 0583 and 0590 are cited by Task 1100 as current Cybernetics Core design-system evidence.

## Scope

- CyberCore frontend scope decision: mirror, companion app, replacement candidate, or ADS consumer only.
- Route parity matrix for current Cybernetics Core frontend/admin surfaces.
- API/data contract inventory for read-only frontend surfaces.
- Fixture-backed Flutter CyberCore app under `warp-prism/apps/cybercore/` once the Melos scaffold exists.
- Pilot screens that consume `packages/warp_prism_ui` and reuse catalog/state matrices.
- CI/test gate that proves ADS changes do not break CyberCore app consumers.

## Out of Scope

- Replacing the current Cybernetics Core Next.js frontend without a later explicit migration decision.
- Live mutation against Cybernetics Core backend APIs before safety and auth gates are documented.
- Reimplementing all Cybernetics Core routes in the first wave.
- Introducing SQLite or client-side durable runtime state.

## RF8 Framing

| Stage | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Goal | Provide a path from reusable Flutter ADS to real Cybernetics Core frontend value. |
| Domain | Cybernetics Core admin/control plane surfaces, registry views, health/status, configuration UX, and governance states. |
| Feature | Scope decision, route parity, API contract, fixture-backed app shell, pilot screens, expansion gate. |
| Representation | Monorepo apps/packages, catalog stories, CyberCore pilot fixtures, route/API matrices. |
| Specs | Typed DTOs/read models, route contracts, operational state vocabulary, fixture schemas. |
| Behaviour | Browse registry/status surfaces read-only, inspect details, show loading/error/empty/degraded states. |
| Test | `melos run analyze`, `melos run test`, app-level widget tests, fixture parser tests, catalog smoke. |
| Eval | No CyberCore route promoted without source-route mapping, fixture, widget test, accessibility/semantics check, and ADS consumer compatibility. |

### Wave 1: Monorepo + Scope (existing)

- Task 1113: Command palette (Cmd+K global search, fuzzy match, action execution).

- Task 1120: Drag-and-drop task board.

- Task 1122: Tab bar + resizable split pane.

# Task 1104: Warp Prism Melos Monorepo Architecture Plan

> **Status**: `[ ]` Open
> **Priority**: 🔴 P0
> **Type**: `architecture` | `governance`
> **Origin**: User clarified ADS reuse/versioning/CI requirements and approved Warp Prism as a parent monorepo with ADS, catalog, and frontend apps as child projects.

---

## Objective

Create the architecture decision and migration plan for restructuring Warp Prism as a Flutter Melos monorepo with reusable `packages/warp_prism_ui`, Storybook/Widgetbook-like `apps/catalog`, current ASW Observatory app under `apps/observatory`, and future CyberCore frontend under `apps/cybercore`. This task must decide package boundaries, CI/test strategy, path dependency policy, and the migration sequence without moving code yet.

## Background Context

### What already exists

- Warp Prism currently has a single Flutter app structure at the child root with `pubspec.yaml`, `lib/`, `test/`, design-system files, app routes, and workspace snapshot features.
- `docs/tasks/00-planning/1100-warp-prism-operational-atomic-design-system-epic.md` calls for reusable `warp_prism_ui` and `warp_prism_catalog`.
- `docs/tasks/01-open/1103-warp-prism-flutter-tooling-and-scaffold.md` proposes `packages/warp_prism_ui` and `apps/warp_prism_catalog`.
- User clarified that ADS upgrades must be visible to consuming frontends with minimal effort and that new frontend ideas should be able to feed reusable atoms/molecules/organisms back into ADS.

### What is missing or broken

- There is no documented package/app boundary for ADS, catalog, observatory, and CyberCore.
- There is no Melos policy or alternative monorepo decision.
- Existing `1101–1103` stale context still assumes `warp-prism/` is empty.
- Without an architecture plan, a builder could either keep ADS too coupled to one app or split it into a repo too early and create update/versioning friction.

- The plan MUST specify package names and paths for ADS, catalog, observatory, and CyberCore app.
- The plan MUST define how ADS changes are validated against all consumers.
- The plan MUST explicitly preserve current Warp Prism work and describe migration sequencing.
- No Flutter code may be moved in this task.

# Task 1116: Warp Prism Notification Toast System

> **Status**: `[ ]` Open
> **Priority**: 🟡 P1
> **Type**: `feature` | `design-system`
> **Origin**: EPIC-11 gap analysis (IMPORTANT GAP-I3)
> **Blocks**: CyberCore mutation screens (future), any screen requiring user feedback
> **Depends on**: Task 1105, Task 1107

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 1116` plus optional slug for
> dependencies, blockers, review ledgers, reports, and architecture references.

---

## Objective

Implement a reusable notification/toast system (`DSToast`, `DSToastManager`, `DSToastSeverity`) for the `warp_prism_ui` design system package with severity coloring (info/success/warning/error), stacking behavior, auto-dismiss with configurable duration, optional action buttons, and a Riverpod integration contract that keeps toast dispatch in a StateNotifier while the toast rendering lives in the DS widget layer. The ADS gap analysis reports a `state-notifier-owns-snackbar` rule but NO reusable widget exists — every screen would need to build ad-hoc snackbar/toast logic.

## Background Context

### What already exists

- The gap analysis report at `docs/reports/ads-gap-analysis-20260608.md` references a `state-notifier-owns-snackbar` rule — the principle that a Riverpod StateNotifier should own dispatching notification events, not the UI widget directly.
- `DSStateSurface` handles empty/loading/error page-level states but has no inline notification or toast capability.
- `DSColors.statusError`, `DSColors.statusHealthy` (assumed from status dot), and accent colors provide the severity color palette.
- `DSMotion` provides animation durations for enter/exit transitions.
- `DSGlassPanel` provides glass-panel container styling with blur and border.
- `DSSpacing`, `DSRadii`, `DSTypography` tokens are available.
- Flutter's `ScaffoldMessenger` and `SnackBar` are framework primitives but lack severity coloring, stacking, and the DS glass aesthetic.
- No `DSToast`, `DSNotification`, `DSToastOverlay`, or `DSToastSeverity` exists anywhere in the codebase.

### What is missing or broken

- No reusable toast/notification widget in `warp_prism_ui`.
- No severity enum with corresponding color/icon mapping.
- No overlay-based stacking manager for multiple simultaneous toasts.
- No auto-dismiss timer with configurable duration per toast.
- No action button support (e.g., "Undo", "View details").
- No Riverpod provider contract documenting how a StateNotifier dispatches toasts.
- No catalog cases for toast variants.

---

## Test Requirements

- `DSToastSeverity` MUST define at least 4 values: `info`, `success`, `warning`, `error`.
- Each severity MUST map to a distinct color from `DSColors` and a distinct icon.
- `DSToast` MUST render a glass-panel styled container with severity left-border accent, icon, title, optional message, and optional action button.
- `DSToastManager` MUST support stacking — multiple toasts render vertically from bottom with gap spacing.
- Auto-dismiss MUST fire after a configurable `duration` (default 4 seconds), with pause-on-hover support.
- Action button MUST trigger a callback and optionally dismiss the toast.
- The Riverpod contract MUST define: a `ToastNotifier` that holds a list of toast entries and provides `show()`/`dismiss()` methods; a `toastListProvider` that the widget layer watches.
- Widget tests MUST cover: render each severity, auto-dismiss fires, action button callback, stacking renders multiple toasts.

---

## Exit Conditions

- [ ] `packages/warp_prism_ui/lib/src/molecules/ds_toast.dart` exists with `DSToast`, `DSToastSeverity`, `DSToastEntry` types.
- [ ] `packages/warp_prism_ui/lib/src/molecules/ds_toast_manager.dart` exists with overlay-based stacking manager.
- [ ] `packages/warp_prism_ui/lib/src/molecules/molecules.dart` exports toast widgets.

# Task 1117: Warp Prism Graph Visualization Refactor And Enhancement

> **Status**: `[ ]` Open
> **Priority**: 🟡 P1
> **Type**: `feature` | `design-system`
> **Origin**: EPIC-11 gap analysis (IMPORTANT GAP-I1)
> **Blocks**: CyberCore dependency visualization, Observatory graph views, future graph features
> **Depends on**: Task 1105, Task 1107, Task 0512

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 1117` plus optional slug for
> dependencies, blockers, review ledgers, reports, and architecture references.

---

## Objective

Refactor the existing `DSGraphCanvas` (483-line monolith at `lib/design_system/organisms/ds_graph_canvas.dart`) into composable layers — graph model, layout engine, painter, interaction handler — and add hierarchical/tree layout, layered DAG layout, graph filtering by node/edge type, a minimap overlay, and node hover preview tooltip. The current monolith mixes data model (`GraphNode`, `GraphEdge`), physics simulation (`_updatePhysics`), painting (`_GraphPainter`), and interaction handling (`GestureDetector`, `MouseRegion`) in a single file. This blocks graph feature growth — adding radial layout, accessibility, edge differentiation, or advanced interactions requires modifying the same 483-line file.

## Background Context

### What already exists

- `DSGraphCanvas` at `lib/design_system/organisms/ds_graph_canvas.dart` (483 lines): a `StatefulWidget` with embedded `GraphNode` class (lines 12-62), `GraphEdge` class (lines 64-77), force-directed physics simulation (lines 141-195), `_GraphPainter` custom painter (lines 382-483), node rendering with `GestureDetector` and `MouseRegion` (lines 296-378), pan/zoom via `GestureDetector.onScaleUpdate`.
- `GraphNode` has fields: `id`, `label`, `type` (agent/skill/workflow/task/doc), `status`, `metadata`, `position`, `velocity`, `isDragging`, `isHovered`, `isSelected`.
- `GraphEdge` has fields: `sourceId`, `targetId`, `label`, `edgeType` (uses/triggers/references).
- `_getNodeColor` maps type to `DSColors.assetAgent`, `assetSkill`, `assetWorkflow`, `assetTask`, `assetReference`.
- `_getNodeIcon` maps type to material icons.
- `_GraphPainter` draws curved edges with quadratic bezier and arrows.
- `DSColors`, `DSSpacing`, `DSRadii`, `DSMotion`, `DSShadows`, `DSStateSurface` tokens/components are available.
- Task 0512 (map graph modes and adapters) in `docs/tasks/02-doing/` provides graph mode context.
- Gap analysis report documents GAP-I1 as IMPORTANT: missing hierarchical/tree layout, layered DAG layout, radial layout, graph filtering, minimap, node hover preview, accessibility, edge differentiation, composability.

### What is missing or broken

- No separate graph model class — `GraphNode` and `GraphEdge` are defined inline in the organism file.
- No layout engine abstraction — force-directed physics is hardcoded in `_updatePhysics`.
- No hierarchical (tree) layout algorithm.
- No layered DAG (Sugiyama-style) layout algorithm.
- `_GraphPainter` is a private class — not testable in isolation.
- No minimap overlay showing the full graph extent with a viewport indicator.
- No node hover preview tooltip (only border color change on hover).
- No graph filtering by node type or edge type.
- No edge differentiation — all edges render identically regardless of `edgeType`.
- No accessibility annotations (semantic labels on nodes/edges).

---

## Test Requirements

- Extracted `GraphModel` class MUST be testable without a widget tree (pure data).
- `ForceDirectedLayout` MUST produce stable positions for a 10-node, 15-edge graph in <100ms.
- `HierarchicalLayout` MUST produce a top-to-bottom tree arrangement with no overlapping nodes.
- `LayeredDagLayout` MUST produce a left-to-right layered arrangement respecting edge direction.
- Extracted `GraphPainter` (public) MUST be testable with `Canvas` mock or `PictureRecorder`.
- `GraphFilter` MUST support filtering by node type, edge type, or both simultaneously.
- Minimap MUST render a scaled-down view of the full graph with a viewport rectangle.
- Node hover preview MUST show a tooltip with label, type, status, and metadata summary.
- Widget tests MUST cover: model construction, each layout algorithm output, painter draws edges, filter removes correct nodes/edges.

---

## Exit Conditions

- [ ] `packages/warp_prism_ui/lib/src/organisms/graph/graph_model.dart` exists with `GraphModel`, `GraphNode`, `GraphEdge`, `GraphNodeId`, `GraphEdgeId` typed IDs.

### How

2. Extract `graph_model.dart` from the monolith — pure data classes, no Flutter dependency.

5. Implement `layered_dag_layout.dart` using Sugiyama — cycle removal, layer assignment, crossing minimization, coordinate assignment.
6. Extract `graph_painter.dart` from `_GraphPainter` — make public, add edge type differentiation, accept style config.
7. Implement `graph_filter.dart` — filter `GraphModel` by allowed types.
8. Implement minimap and hover preview as independent overlay widgets.
9. Refactor `DSGraphCanvas` to compose all layers — the widget becomes a thin orchestrator.
10. Add catalog cases and tests.
11. Run `melos run analyze` and `melos run test`.
12. Add changelog entry.

### Why

The 483-line monolith blocks all graph feature growth. Every new layout algorithm, interaction pattern, or rendering enhancement requires modifying the same file, increasing merge conflict risk and cognitive load. Extracting composable layers enables independent development, testing, and extension of each concern. The hierarchical and layered DAG layouts are required for CyberCore dependency visualization (tasks, agents, skills, workflows have tree/DAG structure that force-directed layout cannot express clearly).

# Task 1118: Warp Prism Operational State Vocabulary Expansion

> **Status**: `[ ]` Open
> **Priority**: 🟡 P1
> **Type**: `design-system` | `architecture`
> **Origin**: EPIC-11 gap analysis (IMPORTANT GAP-I5)
> **Blocks**: Task 1119, CyberCore operational surfaces
> **Depends on**: Task 1105, Task 1102

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 1118` plus optional slug for dependencies, blockers, review ledgers, reports, and architecture references.

---

## Objective

Expand the `DSStateType` enum from its current 3 states (`empty`, `loading`, `error`) to a 14+ operational state vocabulary that covers the full CyberCore domain surface. The expanded vocabulary must include color token mapping per state, icon mapping per state, behavioral contracts (which states allow user actions, which are terminal, which show warnings), and state transition rules per entity type. This vocabulary becomes the canonical state reference for all downstream DS components (health cards, status dots, badges, task cards, detail inspectors, data tables).

## Background Context

### What already exists
- `DSStateType` enum in `lib/design_system/molecules/ds_state_surface.dart` with 3 states: `empty`, `loading`, `error`.
- `DSStatusDot` in `lib/design_system/atoms/ds_status_dot.dart` with 5 named constructors: `success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`, `neutral`.
- `DSBadge` in `lib/design_system/atoms/ds_badge.dart` with `success`, `warning`, `error`, `info` variants.
- Task 1102 inventory defines the target vocabulary: healthy, degraded, error, disabled, pending, running, approved, rejected, redacted, exposed, stale, unverified, promoted, archived.
- The Go backend has 11 state machines (capability lifecycle, circuit breaker, plugin lifecycle, policy lifecycle, etc.) documented in `docs/reference/cybercore-backend-features/`.
- Gap analysis report at `docs/reports/ads-gap-analysis-20260608.md` identifies GAP-I5.

### What is missing or broken
- `DSStateType` only covers data-fetch states, not operational lifecycle states.
- No mapping exists between backend Go state machines and frontend DS state vocabulary.
- No behavioral contract defines which states allow edit actions, which are read-only terminals, which require warnings.
- No transition rules define valid state changes (e.g., `pending` → `running` → `approved` but NOT `archived` → `running`).
- `DSStatusDot` and `DSBadge` use ad-hoc color selection rather than a canonical state-to-color mapping.
- No documentation artifact captures the complete state vocabulary with all semantic relationships.

---

## Test Requirements

- The expanded enum MUST contain at least 14 distinct operational states.
- Each state MUST have exactly one assigned color token from `DSColors`.
- Each state MUST have exactly one assigned Material icon code point.
- A behavioral contract table MUST classify each state as: allows-actions (boolean), is-terminal (boolean), shows-warning (boolean), severity-level (enum).
- State transition rules MUST define valid next-states per entity type (at minimum: capability, circuit-breaker, plugin, policy, task).
- The existing `DSStateSurface` named constructors (`empty`, `loading`, `error`) MUST continue to work without breaking changes.
- `DSStatusDot` MUST gain named constructors for all new states or a factory that accepts `DSOperationalState`.
- `DSBadge` MUST gain a factory or named constructors that accept `DSOperationalState`.
- Widget tests MUST verify color and icon mapping for every state.
- Widget tests MUST verify that existing `DSStateSurface.empty/loading/error` usage is unaffected.

---

## Exit Conditions

- [ ] `DSOperationalState` enum (or expanded `DSStateType`) exists in `lib/design_system/` with ≥14 states, color mapping, and icon mapping.
- [ ] Color token mapping table is documented in code comments and in a design doc under `docs/design/`.
- [ ] Behavioral contract table is documented (allowed-actions, is-terminal, shows-warning per state).
- [ ] State transition rules are documented per entity type.
- [ ] `DSStatusDot` updated to accept `DSOperationalState` or gains new named constructors.
- [ ] `DSBadge` updated to accept `DSOperationalState` or gains a factory constructor.
- [ ] `DSStateSurface` convenience constructors still work (no breaking change).
- [ ] Gallery/catalog cases exist demonstrating all operational states.
- [ ] `melos run analyze` passes (or `flutter analyze` if pre-Melos).
- [ ] `melos run test` passes with ≥14 widget tests covering state rendering.
- [ ] Local changelog entry added under `docs/changelog/`.
- [ ] Completion Evidence is filled before review handoff.

---

## Details

### What

Subtasks:

- [ ] **Read existing code before modifying**: read `lib/design_system/molecules/ds_state_surface.dart`, `lib/design_system/atoms/ds_status_dot.dart`, `lib/design_system/atoms/ds_badge.dart`, `lib/design_system/tokens/ds_colors.dart`, Task 1102 outputs at `docs/tasks/01-open/1102-warp-prism-control-surface-inventory.md`, the operational state vocabulary doc if it exists under `docs/design/`, the Go backend state machines in `docs/reference/cybercore-backend-features/`, and the gap analysis at `docs/reports/ads-gap-analysis-20260608.md`.
- [ ] Define the `DSOperationalState` enum with all 14+ states: `healthy`, `degraded`, `error`, `disabled`, `pending`, `running`, `approved`, `rejected`, `redacted`, `exposed`, `stale`, `unverified`, `promoted`, `archived`. Add `empty`, `loading` as data-fetch-only aliases if they remain needed separately.
- [ ] Define color token mapping: map each `DSOperationalState` to a `DSColors` constant. Reuse existing status colors where semantically correct (healthy→statusSuccess, error→statusError, degraded→statusWarning). Introduce new colors only where existing tokens are insufficient (e.g., `stale` might use a muted amber, `redacted` might use a dim violet).
- [ ] Define icon mapping: map each `DSOperationalState` to a single Material `IconData` constant. Use recognizable icons (healthy→check_circle, error→error_outline, disabled→block, pending→schedule, running→sync, etc.).
- [ ] Define behavioral contract table in code and in `docs/design/operational-state-behavioral-contracts.md`:
  - `allowsActions`: boolean — can the user initiate actions (edit, approve, retry) in this state?
  - `isTerminal`: boolean — is this a final state with no automatic transitions?
  - `showsWarning`: boolean — should UI surfaces display a warning indicator?
  - `severity`: enum { info, success, warning, error, critical } — used for ambient color and notification routing.
- [ ] Define state transition rules per entity type. Create a `docs/design/operational-state-transitions.md` with valid next-states tables for: capability, circuit-breaker, plugin, policy, task, agent, workflow. Minimum 3 entity types must have complete transition tables.
- [ ] Update `DSStatusDot` to support operational states: add a `DSStatusDot.operational(DSOperationalState state)` factory constructor or individual named constructors per state. Preserve existing `success/warning/error/info/neutral` constructors for backward compatibility.
- [ ] Update `DSBadge` to support operational states: add a `DSBadge.operational(DSOperationalState state, {String? label})` factory constructor. Preserve existing constructors.
- [ ] Add gallery/catalog cases showing every operational state in a grid or showcase section.
- [ ] Add widget tests for: each state renders correct color, each state renders correct icon, existing DSStateSurface constructors still work, behavioral contract values are correct for each state.
- [ ] **Simplicity pass**: avoid over-engineering — the enum should be a flat enum with extension methods for color/icon/behavior, not a class hierarchy.
- [ ] **Regression verification**: run `melos run analyze` and `melos run test`.

| `lib/design_system/gallery/design_system_gallery_sections.dart` | Modify — add operational state gallery section. |
| `test/design_system/` | Create — widget tests for operational states. |

### How

1. Read all existing DS state-related code and the Task 1102 inventory to understand the current vocabulary.
2. Read the Go backend feature docs to catalog all state machines and their states.
3. Design `DSOperationalState` as a flat enum with extension methods for `color`, `icon`, `allowsActions`, `isTerminal`, `showsWarning`, and `severity`.
4. Keep `DSStateType` as-is for backward compatibility but make it a subset or alias of the new enum. `DSStateSurface` constructors continue to work.
5. Add new constructors/factories to `DSStatusDot` and `DSBadge`.
6. Document behavioral contracts and transition rules in `docs/design/`.
7. Add gallery showcase and widget tests.
8. Run analyze and test to verify no regressions.

### Why

The 3-state `DSStateType` covers only data-fetch scenarios. CyberCore has 11 backend state machines with 14+ distinct operational states. Without a canonical frontend vocabulary, every DS component will invent its own ad-hoc state handling, leading to visual inconsistency, broken behavioral contracts, and unmaintainable switch statements across the entire ADS. This task is a prerequisite for Task 1119 (Health Dashboard) and all CyberCore operational surfaces.
