# Task 1119: Warp Prism Health Dashboard Components

> **Status**: `[ ]` Open
> **Priority**: 🟡 P1
> **Type**: `feature` | `design-system`
> **Origin**: EPIC-11 gap analysis (IMPORTANT GAP-I4)
> **Blocks**: CyberCore system health screens
> **Depends on**: Task 1105, Task 1107, Task 1118

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 1119` plus optional slug for dependencies, blockers, review ledgers, reports, and architecture references.

---

## Objective

Implement a suite of health dashboard components for `warp_prism_ui` that cover CyberCore system monitoring surfaces: `DSHealthCard` (compound health indicator combining service name, operational state, latency, uptime percentage, and trend sparkline), `DSStatusGrid` (responsive grid showing health of 50+ services simultaneously — MCP servers, agents, workflows), `DSUptimeBar` (horizontal bar visualizing uptime percentage with threshold coloring), and `DSSparkline` (inline mini-chart for trend visualization). These components compose existing atoms (`DSStatusDot`, `DSBadge`, `DSMetricTile`) with the expanded `DSOperationalState` vocabulary from Task 1118 to form a complete health monitoring surface.

## Background Context

### What already exists
- `DSStatusDot` in `lib/design_system/atoms/ds_status_dot.dart` — atomic colored status indicator with animation.
- `DSMetricTile` and `DSMetricTileCompact` in `lib/design_system/molecules/ds_metric_tile.dart` — numeric metric display with label, value, optional trend arrow, and glass-panel styling.
- `DSGlassPanelSimple` in `lib/design_system/atoms/ds_glass_panel.dart` — glass-panel container.
- `DSTrend` enum (`up`, `down`, `flat`) in `ds_metric_tile.dart` — basic trend direction.
- `DSStateSurface` in `lib/design_system/molecules/ds_state_surface.dart` — empty/loading/error states.
- `DSBadge` in `lib/design_system/atoms/ds_badge.dart` — status badges.
- `DSColors` token set includes status colors (`statusSuccess`, `statusWarning`, `statusError`, `statusInfo`).
- The gap analysis report (`docs/reports/ads-gap-analysis-20260608.md`) identifies GAP-I4: health dashboard is partial — `DSStatusDot` + `DSMetricTile` exist but are too primitive for a real health dashboard.

### What is missing or broken
- No compound health card widget that combines service name + operational state + latency + uptime + trend in a single glanceable card.
- No status grid/matrix widget that can render 50+ service health cards in a responsive grid layout.
- No uptime bar widget that visualizes uptime percentage as a horizontal bar with threshold coloring (green >99%, yellow >95%, red <95%).
- No sparkline/mini-chart widget for inline trend visualization (latency over time, error rate over time).
- `DSTrend` is a 3-value enum (up/down/flat) — insufficient for actual data-point trend rendering.
- No CyberCore system health screen can be built with existing primitives alone.

---

## Test Requirements

- `DSHealthCard` MUST display: service name, operational state indicator, latency value with unit, uptime percentage, and a sparkline trend.
- `DSHealthCard` MUST accept a `DSOperationalState` from Task 1118 to determine color and icon.
- `DSStatusGrid` MUST render a responsive grid of `DSHealthCard` widgets that wraps based on available width.
- `DSStatusGrid` MUST support filtering by operational state (show only errored services, show all, etc.).
- `DSStatusGrid` MUST handle 50+ items without performance degradation (use `GridView.builder` with lazy rendering).
- `DSUptimeBar` MUST render a horizontal bar where fill width represents uptime percentage.
- `DSUptimeBar` MUST color-code based on thresholds: green (>99%), amber (>95%), red (<95%).
- `DSUptimeBar` MUST display the uptime percentage as text label.
- `DSSparkline` MUST render an inline mini-chart from a list of numeric data points.
- `DSSparkline` MUST support min 5 and max 100+ data points.
- `DSSparkline` MUST use the accent color from the associated operational state or a provided color override.
- All new widgets MUST have semantic labels for accessibility.
- Widget tests MUST cover: health card rendering, grid layout, uptime bar thresholds, sparkline data rendering, empty data handling.

2. Implement bottom-up: `DSSparkline` (atom) → `DSUptimeBar` (molecule) → `DSHealthCard` (molecule) → `DSStatusGrid` (organism).

6. `DSStatusGrid` uses `GridView.builder` with `SliverGridDelegateWithMaxCrossAxisExtent` for responsive wrapping.
7. All widgets accept null/empty data gracefully and render appropriate empty states.
8. Add gallery showcase and widget tests.
9. Run analyze and test to verify.

### Why

CyberCore needs system health monitoring for 50+ MCP servers, 10+ agents, and 8+ workflows. The existing `DSMetricTile` shows a single number; `DSStatusDot` shows a single colored dot. Neither provides the compound, glanceable health overview required for operational dashboards. Without these components, every CyberCore health screen will build ad-hoc implementations that miss glass-panel aesthetics, accessibility, and the operational state vocabulary from Task 1118.

# Task 1120: Warp Prism Drag And Drop Task Board

> **Status**: `[ ]` Open
> **Priority**: 🟡 P1
> **Type**: `feature` | `design-system`
> **Origin**: EPIC-11 gap analysis (IMPORTANT GAP-I7)
> **Blocks**: Operate workspace interactivity
> **Depends on**: Task 1105, Task 1107

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 1120` plus optional slug for dependencies, blockers, review ledgers, reports, and architecture references.

---

## Objective

Add drag-and-drop interactivity to the existing `DSLaneBoard` kanban organism. The current board renders task cards in lanes but has zero drag-and-drop support — cards are static. This task implements `DSDraggableCard` (a wrapper that makes any `DSTaskCard` draggable), `DSDropTarget` (a wrapper that makes lane columns accept drops), reorder within the same lane, move between different lanes, and visual feedback (ghost card during drag, drop zone highlight when a valid target is hovered). The implementation must use Flutter's built-in `Draggable`/`DragTarget` widgets and integrate with the existing glass-panel aesthetic.

## Background Context

### What already exists
- `DSLaneBoard` in `lib/design_system/organisms/ds_lane_board.dart` — kanban board with horizontal lane columns, each containing a `ListView.builder` of `DSTaskCard` widgets. Supports `onTaskTap` callback but NO drag-and-drop.
- `DSTaskCard` in `lib/design_system/molecules/ds_task_card.dart` — task card with ID, title, lane, priority, owner, proof state, review score, linked skills, dependency count. Supports tap and keyboard focus but NO drag handle or drag behavior.
- `DSLane` data class with `id`, `label`, and `List<DSLaneTask> tasks`.
- `DSLaneTask` data class with `id`, `title`, `priority`, `owner`, `proofState`, `reviewScore`, `linkedSkills`, `dependencyCount`.
- `DSColors`, `DSSpacing`, `DSRadii`, `DSMotion` tokens for visual consistency.
- `DSStateSurface` for empty lane states.
- The gap analysis report (`docs/reports/ads-gap-analysis-20260608.md`) identifies GAP-I7: `DSLaneBoard` has no drag-and-drop.

### What is missing or broken
- No `DSDraggableCard` wrapper exists to make `DSTaskCard` draggable.
- No `DSDropTarget` wrapper exists to make lane columns accept drops.
- No reorder-within-lane logic exists.
- No move-between-lanes logic exists.
- No visual feedback exists: no ghost card during drag, no drop zone highlight, no insertion indicator.
- `DSLane` and `DSLaneTask` are immutable data classes with no mutation callbacks for reorder/move.
- The Operate workspace in CyberCore needs an interactive task board, not just a read-only renderer.

---

## Test Requirements

- `DSDraggableCard` MUST wrap `DSTaskCard` and make it draggable via long-press or drag handle.
- `DSDraggableCard` MUST render a ghost card (semi-transparent, reduced opacity) at the drag origin during drag.
- `DSDropTarget` MUST wrap lane column content and accept `DSDraggableCard` drops.
- `DSDropTarget` MUST highlight the lane border/background when a valid drag is hovering over it.
- Reorder within the same lane MUST move the task to the new index in the task list.
- Move between different lanes MUST remove the task from the source lane and insert it at the target lane.
- An insertion indicator (horizontal line or gap) MUST show where the task will be placed within a lane.
- The callback API MUST notify the parent of reorder/move events: `onReorder(String laneId, int oldIndex, int newIndex)` and `onMove(String sourceLaneId, String targetLaneId, int taskId, int targetIndex)`.
- Keyboard accessibility: drag-and-drop MUST NOT break existing keyboard navigation and tap behavior of `DSTaskCard`.
- Widget tests MUST cover: drag start renders ghost, drop on same lane triggers reorder, drop on different lane triggers move, drop zone highlight appears on hover, empty lane accepts drop.

---

## Exit Conditions

- [ ] `DSDraggableCard` widget exists in `lib/design_system/molecules/` (or `packages/warp_prism_ui/lib/src/molecules/` post-Melos).
- [ ] `DSDropTarget` widget exists in `lib/design_system/molecules/` (or `packages/warp_prism_ui/lib/src/molecules/` post-Melos).
- [ ] `DSLaneBoard` is updated to use `DSDraggableCard` and `DSDropTarget` internally.
- [ ] `DSLaneBoard` accepts `onReorder` and `onMove` callbacks.
- [ ] Visual feedback exists: ghost card at drag origin, drop zone highlight on target lane, insertion indicator within lane.
- [ ] Gallery/catalog cases exist demonstrating: drag within lane, drag between lanes, empty lane drop.
- [ ] `melos run analyze` passes (or `flutter analyze` if pre-Melos).

### What

- [ ] Implement `DSDraggableCard` molecule: wraps a `DSTaskCard` in a `LongPressDraggable<DSDragPayload>`. Renders the original card normally. Provides a `feedback` widget (the card rendered at 0.8 opacity with a cyan glow border, sized to match the original). Provides a `childWhenDragging` widget (the card rendered at 0.2 opacity as a ghost placeholder). Preserves existing tap and keyboard behavior on the non-dragged card.

- [ ] Implement drop zone highlight: when `DragTarget` is being hovered (`candidateData.isNotEmpty`), animate the lane container border color from `borderSubtle` to `accentCyan` at 0.3 opacity using `DSMotion.fast`.

- [ ] **Simplicity pass**: use Flutter's built-in `Draggable`/`DragTarget` — do NOT add drag-and-drop packages. Keep the implementation focused on the 3 core behaviors: drag, drop, visual feedback. No animations beyond what DSMotion provides.

### How

3. Implement `DSDraggableCard` using `LongPressDraggable<DSDragPayload>` — long-press to start drag to avoid conflict with tap. Ghost card uses `Opacity(opacity: 0.2)` on the original card. Feedback card uses `Opacity(opacity: 0.8)` + cyan glow `BoxShadow`.

The current `DSLaneBoard` is a read-only renderer — it displays cards but cannot be interacted with via drag-and-drop. Without this capability, the Operate workspace is a static dashboard rather than a usable workflow tool. This task brings the kanban board from "display" to "interactive" using Flutter's built-in drag primitives.

# Task 1122: Warp Prism Tab Bar And Split Pane

> **Status**: `[ ]` Open
> **Priority**: 🔵 P2
> **Type**: `feature` | `design-system`
> **Origin**: EPIC-11 gap analysis (NICE-TO-HAVE GAP-N2 + GAP-N3)

> **Depends on**: Task 1105, Task 1107

> [!IMPORTANT]

---

## Objective

Implement a proper `DSTabBar` with closeable tabs, scrollable overflow, tab badges, and glass-panel aesthetic, plus a `DSSplitPane` with a draggable resizable divider and configurable min/max constraints. Currently the DS uses `DSFilterChipGroup` for tab-like switching (not real tabs) and `MasterDetailTemplate` uses a fixed `Expanded(flex: 3)/Expanded(flex: 2)` ratio — neither satisfies CyberCore multi-view workspace requirements.

## Background Context

### What already exists

- `DSFilterChipGroup` handles toggle-chip selection but lacks tab semantics (closeable, scrollable overflow, badge counts, tab content binding).
- `MasterDetailTemplate` provides a two-pane layout but uses a fixed `Expanded(flex: 3)/Expanded(flex: 2)` split with no user-adjustable divider.
- `DSShell` provides the page-level chrome (topbar, sidebar) that the tab bar will sit inside.
- `DSTopbar` already renders `_Breadcrumbs` — the tab bar will coexist with or replace this for page-level tabs.
- Glass-panel aesthetic: obsidian-dark surfaces, subtle borders, restrained accent highlights.

### What is missing or broken

- No `DSTabBar`, `DSTab`, `DSTabController`, or `DSTabView` exists in the DS.
- No `DSSplitPane`, `DSSplitDivider`, or resizable divider widget exists.
- CyberCore needs: agent workspace with multiple open agent detail tabs, skill editor with code + preview split, task detail with properties + timeline split, MCP registry with table + inspector split.
- The gap report identifies GAP-N2 (Real Tab Component) and GAP-N3 (Resizable Split Pane) as NICE-TO-HAVE.

---

## Test Requirements

- `DSTabBar` MUST support closeable tabs with an `onClose` callback per tab.
- `DSTabBar` MUST support scrollable overflow when tabs exceed available width (horizontal scroll with fade indicators or arrow buttons).
- `DSTabBar` MUST support badge counts on individual tabs (e.g., unread count, error count).
- `DSTabBar` MUST support active tab highlighting with glass-panel accent styling.
- `DSTabController` MUST manage tab state: active index, add/close/reorder operations.
- `DSSplitPane` MUST support a draggable divider between two child panes.
- `DSSplitPane` MUST support configurable minimum and maximum constraints per pane (e.g., min 200px, max 70%).
- `DSSplitPane` MUST support horizontal and vertical orientation.
- `DSSplitPane` MUST render the divider with a visible drag handle that matches the glass-panel aesthetic.
- Widget tests MUST cover: tab open/close/select, scroll overflow, badge rendering, split pane drag, min/max constraints, orientation.

---

### What

# Task 1123: Warp Prism Virtual Scroll Optimization

> **Status**: `[ ]` Open
> **Priority**: 🔵 P2
> **Type**: `feature` | `performance`
> **Origin**: EPIC-11 gap analysis (NICE-TO-HAVE GAP-N4)
> **Blocks**: MCP server registry scale (1400+ rows)
> **Depends on**: Task 1105, Task 1107, Task 1112

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 1123` plus optional slug for dependencies, blockers, review ledgers, reports, and architecture references.

---

## Objective

Implement `DSVirtualList` and `DSVirtualGrid` widgets optimized for 10K+ items with configurable `itemExtent`, `cacheExtent`, and windowed rendering. These build on Task 1112 (Data Table) to ensure the MCP server registry (1400+ rows), audit log (potentially 10K+ entries), and other large-scale CyberCore listings render at 60fps without frame drops. Additionally, provide a performance benchmark test suite that proves the 10K+ row target is met.

## Background Context

### What already exists

- Flutter's built-in `ListView.builder` and `GridView.builder` provide basic virtualization (only build visible children + cache extent).
- Task 1112 (Data Table Component) will create `DSDataTable` — this task extends that component with explicit virtual scroll configuration.
- `DSStateSurface` handles empty/loading/error states for the list boundary conditions.
- No explicit performance configuration API exists in the current DS for controlling cache extent, item extent, or windowed rendering at scale.

### What is missing or broken

- No `DSVirtualList`, `DSVirtualGrid`, or `DSVirtualScrollConfig` exists in the DS.
- No performance benchmark test exists that validates 10K+ row rendering at acceptable frame times.
- `ListView.builder` defaults are acceptable for hundreds of items but may exhibit frame drops at 10K+ without explicit `itemExtent` and `cacheExtent` tuning.
- The MCP server registry has 1400+ rows today; the audit log and capability registry could exceed 10K entries in production.
- The gap report identifies GAP-N4 (Virtual Scroll) as NICE-TO-HAVE — explicit configuration for extreme scale.

---

## Test Requirements

- `DSVirtualList` MUST support configurable `itemExtent` for fixed-height items (enables O(1) scroll offset computation).
- `DSVirtualList` MUST support configurable `cacheExtent` (number of off-screen items to keep in the widget tree).
- `DSVirtualList` MUST support variable-height items when `itemExtent` is null (falls back to standard `ListView.builder` behavior).
- `DSVirtualGrid` MUST support configurable `crossAxisCount` and `cacheExtent`.
- `DSVirtualList` MUST integrate with `DSDataTable` from Task 1112 (the table body should use `DSVirtualList` internally).
- A performance benchmark test MUST demonstrate that 10,000+ items render without exceeding 16ms frame time budget per frame (60fps target).
- The benchmark MUST report: total build time, average frame time, 99th percentile frame time, and peak memory delta.
- Widget tests MUST cover: fixed extent items, variable extent items, cache extent variation, empty list, single item, grid layout.

---

## Exit Conditions

- [ ] `packages/warp_prism_ui/lib/src/organisms/virtual_scroll/` exists with `DSVirtualList`, `DSVirtualGrid`, and `DSVirtualScrollConfig`.
- [ ] `DSVirtualList` supports configurable `itemExtent` and `cacheExtent`.
- [ ] `DSVirtualGrid` supports configurable `crossAxisCount` and `cacheExtent`.
- [ ] `DSDataTable` from Task 1112 uses `DSVirtualList` for its body rendering.
- [ ] Performance benchmark test exists at `packages/warp_prism_ui/test/performance/virtual_scroll_benchmark.dart` proving 10K+ items at 60fps.
- [ ] `apps/catalog/` has catalog cases for virtual list (1K, 5K, 10K items) and virtual grid (1K, 5K items).
- [ ] `melos run analyze` passes with zero new warnings.
- [ ] `melos run test` passes with widget tests and benchmark test.
- [ ] Local changelog entry added under `docs/changelog/`.
- [ ] Completion Evidence is filled before review handoff.

---

## Details

### What

Subtasks:

- [ ] **Read existing code before modifying**: read `packages/warp_prism_ui/lib/src/` structure, all existing `DS*` components, Task 1112 data table implementation, `docs/reports/ads-gap-analysis-20260608.md`, and Task 1105 token/catalog policy.
- [ ] Design `DSVirtualScrollConfig` data class: `itemExtent` (double?), `cacheExtent` (double, default 250.0), `addAutomaticKeepAlives` (bool), `addRepaintBoundaries` (bool), `addSemanticIndexes` (bool).
- [ ] Implement `DSVirtualList` as a `StatelessWidget` wrapping `ListView.builder` with explicit `itemExtent` and `cacheExtent` parameters. When `itemExtent` is provided, use it directly for O(1) scroll offset computation. When null, pass through to default variable-height behavior.
- [ ] Implement `DSVirtualGrid` as a `StatelessWidget` wrapping `GridView.builder` with configurable `crossAxisCount`, `childAspectRatio`, and `cacheExtent`.
- [ ] Integrate `DSVirtualList` into `DSDataTable` (from Task 1112) as the body renderer — the table body should use `DSVirtualList` with a known row extent for fixed-height rows.
- [ ] Create performance benchmark test at `packages/warp_prism_ui/test/performance/virtual_scroll_benchmark.dart`: generate 10,000 mock items, measure widget build time, scroll through all items measuring frame times, report average and p99 frame time, verify all frames < 16ms.
- [ ] Create a second benchmark comparing `DSVirtualList` (with `itemExtent`) vs plain `ListView.builder` (without explicit extent) at 10K items to demonstrate the improvement.
- [ ] Add catalog cases in `apps/catalog/`: one page for `DSVirtualList` (1K fixed-height items, 5K variable-height items, 10K fixed-height items with item count indicator) and one page for `DSVirtualGrid` (1K items, 5K items).
- [ ] Add widget tests: fixed extent, variable extent, cache extent variation, empty list, single item, grid layout, scroll position preservation on rebuild.
- [ ] **Simplicity pass**: no custom `SliverChildDelegate` or custom `RenderSliverList` — wrap Flutter's built-in builders with configuration, not replace them.
- [ ] **Regression verification**: run `melos run analyze` and `melos run test`.

### How

2. Design `DSVirtualScrollConfig` as a simple data class with sensible defaults.

8. Run Melos analyze/test, fix any issues, fill Completion Evidence.

### Why

The MCP server registry has 1400+ rows today and the audit log could exceed 10K entries. Flutter's `ListView.builder` defaults are tuned for typical mobile lists (hundreds of items). Without explicit `itemExtent` (which enables O(1) scroll offset calculation) and `cacheExtent` tuning, the registry and audit log will exhibit frame drops during fast scrolling on desktop. This task provides the DS-level configuration surface to ensure all large-scale CyberCore listings maintain 60fps.

Completion means the repository has a concrete startup path instead of an implied one, and later tasks can build on a real app skeleton rather than inventing entrypoints ad hoc.

## Background Context

### O que já existe:
- `warp-prism/pubspec.yaml` declares a Flutter application and already depends on `go_router`.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/organisms/ds_shell.dart` defines the real shell contract currently available to compose an application frame.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/templates/master_detail_template.dart` shows the intended application structure, even though parts of its current API usage do not match the implemented organisms.

### O que está faltando / quebrado:
- `warp-prism/lib/main.dart` does not exist.
- `warp-prism/lib/app/app.dart` does not exist.
- `warp-prism/lib/app/router.dart` does not exist.
- There is no authoritative minimal route map for the Flutter app, so future screens would have to guess startup and navigation behavior.

---

## Test Requirements

- DEVE existir um `main.dart` que invoque `runApp` para o app Warp-Prism.

- DEVE existir um router com pelo menos uma rota inicial explícita e sem depender de telas futuras não implementadas.
- DEVE usar placeholders mínimos e locais para conteúdo ainda não implementado, sem puxar telas de epics posteriores.

---

# Task 0012: Warp-Prism Design System API Normalization

> **Status**: `[x]` Done
> **Priority**: 🔴 P0
> **Type**: `remediation`
> **Origin**: EPIC-00 Warp-Prism Foundation and Compile Gate promotion
> **Blocks**: Task 0013 and later template/screen tasks

## Objective

Normalize compile-breaking design-system API mismatches so Warp-Prism source files reference the symbols and parameters that actually exist. Completion means the codebase no longer mixes `DS*` and `Ds*` naming conventions arbitrarily, template files no longer call nonexistent shell parameters, and analyzer failures tied to design-system contract drift are either fixed or explicitly isolated.

## Background Context

### O que já existe:
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/tokens/ds_colors.dart` defines `DSColors` rather than `DsColors`.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/organisms/ds_shell.dart` defines `DSShell`, `DSShellResponsive`, `sidebar`, `topbar`, `content`, `inspector`, and `showInspector`.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/organisms/ds_sidebar.dart` defines `DSSidebar` with `selectedId`, `onItemTap`, and `expanded` instead of the API assumed by templates.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/organisms/ds_topbar.dart` defines `DSTopbar` with `searchBar` and `showSearch` instead of the parameter set assumed by templates.

### O que está faltando / quebrado:
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/templates/master_detail_template.dart` currently references `DsShell`, `DsSidebar`, `DsTopbar`, `DsColors`, and `body:` even though the implemented classes use different names and parameters.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/organisms/ds_graph_canvas.dart` references `DsColors.background`, `DsColors.surface`, `DsColors.border`, `accentGreen`, `accentAmber`, `accentMagenta`, `neutral500`, and `neutral600`, none of which exist in `DSColors` as currently implemented.
- Additional mismatches discovered in Task 0010 must be folded into this task instead of patched ad hoc in unrelated future slices.

# Task 0014: Warp Prism DS Token Contract and Inventory

> **Status**: `[x]` Done

### O que esta faltando / quebrado:

- The token layer does not yet define a canonical Theme bridge for downstream widgets.

### DSTaskCard / DSAssetCard Convergence Decision

DSTaskCard remains as a **separate auxiliary molecule**, NOT converged into DSAssetCard. Rationale:

- DSTaskCard is task-lane-specific: it renders `#id`, priority badge, proof state dot, owner, review score, dependency count, and linked skills — all fields that have no equivalent in the generic DSAssetCard contract.
- DSAssetCard is asset-kind-generic: it renders name, kind icon, description, governance chip, tags, and edge count — applicable to any workspace asset.
- Converging them would either bloat DSAssetCard with task-specific fields or loss task-lane visualization fidelity.
- Both molecules compose the same canonical atoms (DSText, DSIcon, DSChip, DSStatusDot), so they share the design system foundation without duplication.

# Task 0019: Warp Prism Preset Workspace Snapshot Starter

> **Status**: `[x]` Completed
> **Priority**: 🔴 P0
> **Type**: `feature`
> **Origin**: `.opencode/user/warp-prism2.txt` research + user request for immediate workspace visibility utility
> **Blocks**: Task 0020
> **Depends on**: Task 0011, Task 0017

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 0019` when referencing this work from
> later Warp Prism build slices. Lanes such as `02-doing` and `03-review` are
> mutable status, not identity.

---

## Objective

Create the first genuinely useful read-only Warp Prism surface: a route that
scans a preset workspace directory and displays discovered agents, skills,
workflows, tasks, and changelog entries using the existing design system. This
is the "holy shit, this already helps me" moment — a Workspace Snapshot that
works immediately against the Ganthritor root without requiring mock corpus
setup, graph normalization, or EPIC-03 data layer completion.

Completion means a developer can run `flutter run -d linux
--dart-define=ASW_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/home/sephiroth/working/ganthritor` and see a
beautiful read-only dashboard of everything in that workspace.

---

## Background Context

### What already exists

- `warp-prism/pubspec.yaml` declares Flutter, `go_router`, `flutter_riverpod`,
  and the design-system dependencies.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/` contains tokens, atoms, molecules,
  organisms, and templates.
- Task 0011 creates `lib/main.dart`, `lib/app/app.dart`, and
  `lib/app/router.dart`.
- Task 0017 creates the Design System Gallery route.
- `warp-prism/docs/research.md` recommends Phase 1 be "read-only and local:
  scan `.opencode/agents`, `.opencode/skills`, `.opencode/workflows`, `docs/tasks`,
  `docs/changelog`, build a normalized index, expose search/graph/filters."
- `warp-prism/docs/prompt.txt` defines the Overview surface with totals for
  agents, skills, sub-skills, workflows, tasks by lane, changelog entries,
  blockers, review queue, and governance warnings.

### What is missing or broken

- No route exists that reads from a real workspace directory.
- No `WorkspaceSource` abstraction exists to swap between mock bundled data and
  a live local preset path.
- The mock corpus under `assets/mock_workspace/` is the only data source; there
  is no way to point the app at the real Ganthritor workspace.
- No filesystem-scanning service exists for `.opencode/` directories.
- The Overview metrics from Task 0412 require EPIC-03 data layer; this task
  provides an immediate lightweight alternative using direct filesystem scan.

---

## Test Requirements

- The route MUST read from a configurable workspace root via `--dart-define` or
  equivalent runtime configuration, defaulting to `..` (parent directory) when
  running from `warp-prism/`.
- The scanner MUST detect `.opencode/agents/*.md`, `.opencode/skills/*/SKILL.md`,
  `.opencode/workflows/*.md`, and `docs/tasks/**/*.md` without following
  symlinks into parent-canonical surfaces unless explicitly configured.
- The scanner MUST parse YAML frontmatter when present and gracefully handle
  files without frontmatter.
- The scanner MUST distinguish five task lanes: `00-planning`, `01-open`,
  `02-doing`, `03-review`, `04-completed`.
- The scanner MUST detect `docs/changelog/*.md` files.
- The surface MUST render all discovered assets using DS primitives
  (atoms/molecules/organisms) rather than bespoke widget styling.
- The surface MUST show a workspace root path and scan status
  (loading/success/error/empty).
- The surface MUST remain strictly read-only.

---

## Exit Conditions

- [x] A `WorkspaceSource` abstract interface exists under
  `warp-prism/lib/data/sources/`.
- [x] A `PresetLocalWorkspaceSource` implementation exists that reads from a
  configurable root path.
- [x] A `WorkspaceSnapshot` typed aggregate exists under
  `warp-prism/lib/data/models/` returning agents, skills, workflows, tasks by
  lane, changelog entries, and scan metadata.
- [x] A route exists (e.g., `/workspace-snapshot` or integrated as the default
  Overview fallback) that loads the preset source and renders the snapshot.
- [x] The surface shows: workspace root path, scan status, agent count, skill
  count, workflow count, task count by lane, changelog count, and at least one
  card list per asset type.
- [x] `flutter analyze` passes without errors.
- [x] `flutter test` passes with 0 failures for new scanner/repository/route
  tests.

### How

1. Define `WorkspaceSource` as an abstract class with `Future<WorkspaceSnapshot>
   load(String rootPath)`.
2. Implement `PresetLocalWorkspaceSource` using `dart:io` to enumerate files,
   parse frontmatter with the `yaml` package, and return typed results.
3. Use `const String.fromEnvironment('ASW_WORKSPACE_ROOT', defaultValue: '..')`
   to make the root configurable at build time.
4. Wire a Riverpod `AsyncNotifierProvider` that loads the snapshot on route
   entry and exposes loading/success/error states.
5. Compose the page from DS primitives: metric tiles for counts, asset cards
   for lists, lane columns for tasks, status indicators for scan state.
6. Keep the page read-only and mutation-free.
7. Test with a temporary fixture directory containing sample `.opencode/` and
   `docs/` structures.

### Why

The current plan requires EPIC-03 data layer and EPIC-04 product shell before
any useful surface exists. That means weeks of implementation before seeing
anything real. This task provides immediate value by reading from a real
workspace path — the developer's own Ganthritor root — and displaying it
beautifully. It also validates the scanner/parser/repository architecture
against real data before investing in graph normalization, storytelling, and
universal detail views.

# Task 0511: Map catalog tabs, cards, and filter interactions

> **Status**: `[x]` Done
> **Priority**: 🟡 P1
> **Type**: `feature`
> **Origin**: `EPIC-05-warp-prism-map-surface.md` candidate stories for catalog tabs and search/filter/chip interaction
> **Blocks**: Task 0513, Task 0514
> **Depends on**: Task 0510 (`0510-warp-prism-map-workspace-scaffold`)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 0511` plus optional slug for dependencies,
> blockers, review ledgers, reports, and architecture references. Lanes such as
> `02-doing` and `03-review` are mutable status, not identity. If a live file path
> is needed, resolve it from `docs/tasks/tasklist.md` or search under `docs/tasks/`.

---

## Objective

Implement the catalog side of the Map surface so users can browse `Agents`, `Skills`, and `Workflows` as DS-composed asset cards with search and filter interactions driven by repository/view-model data rather than static demo lists. Completion means each tab exposes the correct asset family, asset cards surface kind/canonicality/relationship context, and query/filter changes deterministically update the visible result set and empty states.

## Background Context

### O que já existe:
- `warp-prism/docs/prompt.txt` requires Map tabs, asset cards, and relationships for agents, skills, workflows, scripts, references, tasks, and changelog entries.
- `warp-prism/docs/research.md` recommends a synchronized catalog + graph + detail model, where cards show more than a filename and reveal provenance, triggers, and link density.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/molecules/ds_asset_card.dart`, `ds_search_bar.dart`, and `ds_filter_chip_group.dart` already sketch the core UI molecules for a catalog surface.
- Task 0510 is expected to establish the Map route and feature-local state contract.

### O que está faltando / quebrado:
- There is no actual catalog panel for the Map workspace and no feature module that binds asset data to `DSAssetCard`.

# Task 0512: Map graph modes and projection adapters

> **Status**: `[x]` Done
> **Priority**: 🟡 P1
> **Type**: `feature`
> **Origin**: `EPIC-05-warp-prism-map-surface.md` candidate stories for containment, operational, and evidence graph modes
> **Blocks**: Task 0513, Task 0514
> **Depends on**: Task 0510 (`0510-warp-prism-map-workspace-scaffold`), `EPIC-03-warp-prism-data-layer-graph-backbone.md`

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Task identity is lane-neutral. Use `Task 0512` plus optional slug for dependencies,
> blockers, review ledgers, reports, and architecture references. Lanes such as
> `02-doing` and `03-review` are mutable status, not identity. If a live file path
> is needed, resolve it from `docs/tasks/tasklist.md` or search under `docs/tasks/`.

---

## Objective

Implement the Graph subview of the Map surface so the same normalized asset corpus can be projected into three explicit graph modes: `containment`, `operational`, and `evidence`. Completion means the Graph tab can switch among those modes, each mode derives nodes and edges from normalized asset relationships instead of hardcoded demo lists, and the projection contract is test-covered independently from the canvas widget.

## Background Context

### O que já existe:
- `warp-prism/docs/prompt.txt` requires three graph modes and a normalized edge model (`contains`, `routesTo`, `dependsOn`, `references`, `changedBy`, `proves`, `uses`).
- `warp-prism/docs/research.md` explicitly identifies graph mode switching as the differentiator of the Harness Map.
- `warp-prism/lib/design_system/organisms/ds_graph_canvas.dart` already provides a graph canvas organism, but it currently uses a simplified string `type` and local `GraphNode`/`GraphEdge` model.
- Task 0510 is expected to provide the Graph subview entrypoint and feature-local state shell.

### O que está faltando / quebrado:
- No projection layer currently maps normalized workspace assets/edges into graph-mode-specific nodes and links.
- `ds_graph_canvas.dart` still reflects an older asset taxonomy (`agent`, `skill`, `workflow`, `task`, `doc`) and references token names that do not exist, so it cannot yet be trusted as the source of projection truth.
- No tests prove that different graph modes are built from the same source asset graph with different edge selection rules.
- The epic acceptance criteria explicitly forbid manually hardcoded relationship lists, but the current codebase has no guardrail enforcing that boundary.

---

## Test Requirements

- DEVE projetar os mesmos assets normalizados em pelo menos três modos de grafo: `containment`, `operational`, e `evidence`.
- DEVE derivar edges por regra de modo a partir do backbone normalizado, não por listas locais manualmente mantidas no widget.
- DEVE expor contagens e/ou labels de nós/arestas que permitam verificar o modo ativo em testes determinísticos.
- DEVE ter pelo menos um teste happy-path cobrindo troca de modo e um edge case com assets sem arestas elegíveis para um modo específico.

---

## Exit Conditions (GDD/TDD)

- [ ] Existe uma camada de projeção/adaptação do backbone Map para `containment`, `operational`, e `evidence`.
- [ ] O Graph subview alterna entre os três modos sem trocar de fonte de dados.
- [ ] `DsGraphCanvas` ou seu adaptador passa a aceitar o modelo necessário para a feature sem depender de listas hardcoded no widget.
- [ ] Existe pelo menos um teste de unidade/widget cobrindo troca de modo e um caso sem edges elegíveis.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` passa sem erros
- [ ] `flutter test test/features/map/` passa com 0 falhas
- [ ] Entrada de changelog adicionada via engine em `docs/changelog/`

# Task 0610: Warp-Prism Operate Task Projection Contract

> **Priority**: 🔴 P0

## Objective

Define the Operate-specific read model that converts markdown task files from the five canonical lanes into a single projection contract consumable by the Execution Ledger. Completion means the repo has a parser-tested task projection that exposes lane, owner, proof state, review score, dependencies, blockers, linked skills/workflows, validation commands, evidence summary, and markdown sections without relying on the legacy `mock_workspace/.opencode/tasks/queue.md` format.

### O que está faltando / quebrado:
